goal:
Roll out 0.2.x runners and run fleet before/after interrupt recount (S5).

Source research: task 2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4 ("noticing a high level of interruptions"). Read docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/RESPONSE.md, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md and the cited GUIDE before coding. Survey answers (if any) live in docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/RESPONSE_SURVEY.md. Section: RESPONSE.md S5, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/GUIDE-05-commit-push-crash-loop.md (E5 sweep), WIDE_NET Cause 5 + rollout. Survey: q9 (gradual rollout, never force-restart mid-task). Ops + verification, no new unit tests.

Evidence: "Deployed runners are 0.1.0 (main f430f53, 11-11); repo is 0.2.0 with interrupt reasons and deterministic-git-failure handling (046a6391, merged 11-21 09:38 in 7ac148ce). Rollout is backend-nudged, at most daily per runner, idle-converge (docs/runner-update-runbook.md), so lag is expected - but until it lands, every new interrupt is still bare and every commit-hook rejection still crash-loops."

Steps: (1) confirm local-alpha + server2-alpha converge to build containing 046a6391 per docs/runner-update-runbook.md; record GET /runners versions before/after. (2) re-run WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md section 2 counts + GUIDE-07 section 5 fleet script: bare interrupts -> ~0, reasons name Causes 1/3/4, deterministic commit failures surface as FAILED with gitFailure payloads, never interrupts. (3) E5 forensics sweep (GUIDE-05 section 4): for each remaining post-finished interrupt, check kb-<taskId> worktrees (158394ab, db49d6c6, 1cae113f, 7f6220c3) for stage-output-commit presence (present -> Cause 2/4 territory; absent -> Cause 5). Only if E5 finds commit-loop cases 046a6391 does not cover, create a NEW Cause-5 code ticket. (4) record post-rollout counts in task folder as new baseline for S1-S4.

RISK: observe only - do NOT force-restart runners mid-assignment (PROD-ACTION, would create the interrupts being measured). Runs parallel to all code work; only prod CONFIRMATION of S3/S4/S2-runner-half waits on it.

reports.content:
# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — S5: Roll out 0.2.x runners and run fleet before/after interrupt recount

Task: `683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c` (RESPONSE.md S5 of `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4`).
Type: ops + verification. No code changes, no new unit tests.
Date: 2026-11-23. Status: BEFORE + E5 delivered under the q3-fallback
(see `RUN-LOG.md`, `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md`, `E5-SWEEP.md`, `BASELINE.md`);
the AFTER recount is a scheduled follow-up gated on a human PROD-ACTION
(raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the fix-bearing release).

## Goal

Confirm both production runners (`local-alpha`, `server2-alpha`) converge via the
normal idle-update channel to a build containing the deterministic-git-failure fix
(`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in `7ac148ce`), then prove with fleet-wide
before/after counts that the 0.2.x rollout resolves the "bare interrupt" class:
bare interrupts drop to ~0, reasons name Causes 1/3/4, and deterministic commit
failures surface as FAILED completions with `gitFailure` payloads instead of
interrupts. Record the post-rollout counts as the new baseline for S1–S4.

## Success criteria

1. `GET /runners` versions recorded before AND after; both named runners observed
   on a `0.2.x` build whose release contains `046a6391` (verified via
   `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0`, not by version string alone).
2. WIDE_NET §2 counts + GUIDE-07 §5 fleet script re-run on the same scope,
   recorded in the task folder as before/after tables.
3. S5-attributable signals move as predicted: bare interrupts → ~0 on new
   interrupts, `with_reason` names Causes 1/3/4, deterministic commit failures
   appear as FAILED + `gitFailure` (never interrupts). (Cap-escalation and label
   fixes are S1/S6 territory — see §"Attribution boundaries".)
4. E5 forensics sweep (GUIDE-05 §4) executed for every remaining post-`finished`
   interrupt: each classified commit-present (Cause 2/4) or commit-absent
   (Cause 5 suspect), with evidence or an explicit evidence-gap note.
5. Post-rollout baseline recorded in the task folder and usable by S1–S4 as their
   "before" reference (counts + runner versions + backend build + window dates).
6. Zero forced restarts, zero reaped exhibit worktrees, zero agent re-runs:
   observe-only throughout (q9 constraint).

## Grounded facts (verified 2026-11-23 in this checkout)

- HEAD is `7ac148ce` and contains `046a6391` (verified: `git merge-base
  --is-ancestor 046a6391 HEAD` → YES). `046a6391` is the 17-file
  deterministic-git-failure change (daemon branch, `shared/gitFailure/*`).
- `runner/version.json` reads `runnerVersion: 0.2.0`.
  **CORRECTED 2026-11-23 (review F1): tag existence ≠ tag content.**
  `runner-v0.2.0` (`8460e4a8`, 2026-11-19) predates the fix (`046a6391`,
  merged 2026-11-21 09:38 in `7ac148ce`):
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0` → NO, and
  `shared/gitFailure.js` is absent at the tag. A NEW tag `runner-v0.2.1`
  (created 2026-11-23 11:30:02Z from main `65580333`) DOES contain the fix
  (merge-base YES, `shared/gitFailure.js` present, `runnerVersion 0.2.1`).
  Remaining rollout gates: the backend recommended knob (still `0.1.0` at
  12:22Z — runbook step 5, human PROD-ACTION) + per-runner idle converge.
  Never move `runner-v0.2.0`; the fleet converges to `0.2.1` (or newer).
- Recommended-knob wiring: `api/config/schema.js` key `runnerRecommendedVersion`
  (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION`), **default `0.1.0`**. The live value
  must be read at execution time — the default alone cannot confirm the rollout
  is switched on (this is survey q1).
- Runner endpoints exist: `GET /runners` → `runnerRegistry.list()` (fleet
  matrix: versions, badges, update status), `GET /runners/monitor`,
  per-runner `pendingCommands`/`requestUpdate` acks (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`).
- Baseline to beat (WIDE_NET §2, project `0fd41821`, 61 tasks, 2026-11-21):
  118 runner-path interrupts (96 local-alpha / 22 server2-alpha), 49 with
  reason (all cap refusals), 69 bare, 99 ≤15 s after `started` (median 4.7 s),
  15 ≥2 min after `started`, 42 death-streak escalations, 0 server-restart
  interrupts, 100 `Auto-resumed after server restart` rows.
- API base for prod reads: `http://192.168.1.206:3100` (`localhost:3100`
  refuses connections from this runner host, per TICKETS doc).
- E5 exhibits are **already absent on this host**: no `kb-158394ab`,
  `kb-db49d6c6`, `kb-1cae113f`, `kb-7f6220c3` under the server2-alpha work
  root (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_WORK_ROOT=/home/server2/.kainbain/runner-work`,
  only 5 unrelated `kb-*` dirs present). The local-alpha host
  (`192.168.1.206`, `~server`) is unchecked — the sweep must check there
  first and treat absence as an evidence gap with fallbacks (§Phase 2).
- GUIDE-05 §4's path `~/.kainbain/kb-$t` is stale for server2-alpha; the real
  layout is `$KAINBAIN_RUNNER_WORK_ROOT/kb-<taskId>*`. Resolve the work root
  per host before sweeping.

## Survey integration (SURVEY.md + RESPONSE_SURVEY.md)

The task survey (`SURVEY.md`, Round 1, stage-1792362077711) is **answered**
(all four recommended options selected); the source survey
(`RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q1–q9) remains unanswered, so q9's recommended option
(gradual rollout, never force-restart mid-task) is held as a hard constraint.
The table below records the effective decision per question, including where
live data overrode an answer (q1) or forced a fallback (q3):

| Q | Recommended assumption (plan default) | Fallback if answered otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| q1 (knob already on?) | **ANSWERED "already set — observe only", FALSIFIED by live data** (knob is `0.1.0` at 09:04/10:36/11:07/11:46/12:22Z; `availableVersions ["0.1.0"]`, no nudges). Task stays observe-only; the raise to `0.2.1` is a human PROD-ACTION recorded as the blocking prerequisite (see `RUN-LOG.md`) | — (answer binds this task to observe-only) |
| q2 (read-only prod access?) | **ANSWERED: full read-only approved** (backend API + runner journals + worktrees on both hosts) — used throughout | n/a (granted) |
| q3 (wait for converge?) | **ANSWERED "wait-and-watch same-run", ADOPTED FALLBACK**: convergence is impossible until the knob is raised (F1/F2), so this run delivers BEFORE + E5 + versions now and the AFTER recount becomes a scheduled follow-up gated on both runners CONVERGED per `bin/runners-snapshot.sh --require-converged`; never "record mid-rollout as after" | n/a (fallback active; see `BASELINE.md` for the follow-up procedure) |
| q4 (recount scope?) | Same project `0fd41821` only, directly comparable to the 11-21 baseline | All-projects: run the same script per project and keep `0fd41821` as the headline comparison table |
| RESPONSE q9 (rollout pace) | **Hard constraint**: gradual idle-converge, never force-restart mid-task | No fallback — any "faster" answer must come from the human explicitly; the plan refuses to include forced restarts on its own authority |

Execution must re-read both survey files for answers before running anything;
an answered survey overrides the assumption row above.

## Approach — make observation easy, then observe

This task changes nothing; its failure mode is fuzzy, non-reproducible numbers.
So Phase 0 ("make change easy") builds all reusable observation tooling first —
frozen scripts, record templates, access checks, and the BEFORE snapshot — and
only then do the time-ordered phases run. Big/volatile evidence comes early:
the BEFORE recount and the E5 sweep run before the convergence wait, because
interrupts keep accruing and worktree exhibits keep getting reaped (all four
E5 seed exhibits are already absent from this host). The long pole — idle
convergence at most daily per runner — waits in Phase 3 without blocking
Phase 1/2 evidence.

Attribution boundaries (what S5 may and may not claim): S1 (cap counting),
S2-backend (413 limit), S4 (transient tolerance), S6 (labels/counts) all change
the same signals. S5's after-recount MUST record the backend build number
(`GET /deploy/status`) and which sibling fixes have landed, and split new
interrupts by timestamp against each runner's converge time. Only interrupts
timestamped after a runner converged to 0.2.x count as "after" for S5.
`escalated` dropping is an S1 signal, not an S5 gate; the S5 gates are bare→~0,
reasons present, and FAILED+`gitFailure` instead of commit-loop interrupts.

## Phase 0 — Setup: tooling, access, knob state, BEFORE snapshot (first)

0.1 Re-read `SURVEY.md` and `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` for answers; record the
    effective decision per question at the top of the run log.
0.2 Access checks (read-only, stop on first refusal and record it):
    `GET /status/observability`, `GET /tasks?projectId=0fd41821` (expect ~61+
    tasks — confirms project id scope for q4), `GET /runners`,
    `GET /deploy/status` (backend build number), journal read on both hosts,
    work-root listing on both hosts.
0.3 Knob state (q1): record live `runnerRecommendedVersion` /
    `runnerMinVersion` (backend config endpoint or operator-read env).
    Under the default assumption do NOT change them; under the q1-fallback,
    raise recommended to `0.2.0` (config only, no restart) and record old→new.
0.4 Freeze the observation kit in this task folder so S1–S4 re-run identically:
    - `bin/fleet-recount.sh` — GUIDE-07 §5 script pinned to the API base +
      project id, plus a `jq -s` aggregation pass emitting the WIDE_NET §2
      table rows (runner_interrupts, with_reason, bare, ≤15 s, ≥2 min,
      auto_resumed, server_restart, escalated, per-runner split).
    - `bin/runners-snapshot.sh` — `GET /runners` raw JSON → timestamped file.
    - `bin/e5-sweep.sh` — corrected E5 loop resolving `$KAINBAIN_RUNNER_WORK_ROOT`
      per host + journal greps (E3 `Backend 413`, E4 502/`fetch failed`,
      hook/commit lines).
    - `RUN-LOG.md` — timestamped run diary (knob values, backend builds,
      converge times, sibling-fix landings).
0.5 BEFORE snapshot (same run as 0.2): save raw `GET /runners` JSON and run the
    fleet script → `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md` (per-task rows + §2 table). This is the
    "before" half of the rollout proof; everything after compares to it.
0.6 Verify release content: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0`
    (must print YES — proves the 0.2.0 release actually carries the fix).

Gate: kit committed in folder, BEFORE counts + BEFORE versions saved, knob
state recorded. All later phases are mechanical re-runs of Phase 0 tooling.

## Phase 1 — BEFORE recount analysis (same data as 0.5, second lens)

1.1 Recompute the WIDE_NET §2 table from the BEFORE snapshot and diff it against
    the 11-21 baseline (new interrupts since 11-21 are expected — runners are
    still 0.1.0; every new one should still be bare, which itself re-confirms
    the "until it lands" premise).
1.2 List every post-`finished` interrupt (≥2 min after `started`, or explicit
    `finished`→interrupt pair) with task id + timestamps — this is the E5
    worklist for Phase 2.
1.3 Confirm the reason vocabulary on new interrupts: cap refusals still reasoned,
    everything else bare. Any *reasoned non-cap* interrupt before convergence
    would contradict the "0.1.0 emits no reasons" premise — flag, don't ignore.

Gate: `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md` holds §2 table + diff vs 11-21 + E5 worklist.

## Phase 2 — E5 forensics sweep (early: exhibits are volatile)

For each post-`finished` interrupt from 1.2 (seeds: `158394ab`, `db49d6c6`,
`1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`, plus any new ones from 1.1):

2.1 Worktree check per host (read-only, never reap): resolve the runner work
    root on that host first, then
    `git -C $WORK_ROOT/kb-<taskId>* log --oneline -3` and look for a
    stage-output commit matching the execution window. Present → Cause 2/4
    territory; absent → Cause 5 suspect. Record exact SHAs or exact absence.
2.2 Journal join (same host, same window): `Runner failed:` line text +
    restart-counter deltas — names hook/commit vs 413 vs 502/fetch-fail.
2.3 Fallback chain when a worktree is absent (already the case on server2-alpha
    for all four seeds): (a) check the sibling host; (b) check `origin` for the
    stage-output SHA (pushed = commit succeeded, Cause 2/4); (c) journal line
    alone; (d) if all absent, record an explicit evidence gap — never guess.
2.4 Verdict per interrupt: Cause-2/4 vs Cause-5-covered-by-`046a6391` vs
    Cause-5-NOT-covered. The third verdict is the ONLY trigger for new code:
    if and only if E5 finds commit-loop cases `046a6391` does not cover
    (a deterministic failure class outside `HOOK_REJECTED`/`COMMIT_FAILED`/
    `MERGE_CONFLICT` that still crash-loops on 0.2.x), file a NEW Cause-5
    code ticket with the journal line + worktree state + failing class.

Gate: `E5-SWEEP.md` with one row per post-`finished` interrupt (evidence or
gap) + the ticket/no-ticket decision with reasoning.

## Phase 3 — Convergence watch (the long pole; observe only)

3.1 Poll `GET /runners` on a slow cadence (30–60 min) and snapshot each poll.
    Per runner record: running version + build facts, `updateAvailable` /
    `belowMinimum` / `updateStatus` badges, pending vs acked `requestUpdate`
    (nudge cooldown is 24 h), busy/idle, pinned-vs-Latest.
3.2 Declare a runner converged at the first poll showing a 0.2.x build whose
    release contains `046a6391`; record the converge timestamp per runner in
    `RUN-LOG.md`. Both converged → proceed to Phase 4 (q3 default).
3.3 If a runner stalls (badge never clears past 24–48 h): triage READ-ONLY per
    the runbook ("a runner says out of date") — `entrypoint: direct` vs
    wrapper, `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` opt-out, pinned version, pin
    older than running, recommended knob above every release, `updateStatus`
    failure reason — and record the blocking cause. Fixes (migrate, flip the
    switch, Update button) are PROD-ACTION: propose, do not perform.
3.4 NEVER to speed convergence: force-restart mid-assignment, Update-on-busy,
    reaping worktrees, re-running parked tasks. Any of these manufactures the
    interrupts being measured (q9 / PROD-ACTION ban).

Gate: per-runner converge timestamps, or a stalled-runner triage note with a
named blocking cause. Under the q3-fallback (before-now/stop), Phase 3 becomes
a scheduled follow-up run instead of a same-run wait.

## Phase 4 — AFTER recount + journal sweeps (after both converge)

4.1 AFTER snapshot: raw `GET /runners` JSON + fleet script → `RECOUNT-AFTER.md`
    (§2 table + per-task rows), timestamped ≥ both converge times.
4.2 Split new interrupts at each runner's converge time; evaluate the S5 gates
    on post-converge interrupts only: bare → ~0; reasons name Causes 1/3/4
    (cap strings, setup-fault messages, transient 502/fetch-fail strings);
    deterministic commit failures arrive as FAILED completions carrying
    `gitFailure` payloads (`kind`/`phase`/`summary`) with NO interrupt row.
4.3 Journal sweeps (both hosts, post-converge window): E3 `Backend 413` lines
    (expect none-new after S2 lands; any 413 on 0.2.x must pair with a FAILED
    completion, never a crash loop), E4 502/`fetch failed` crash lines
    (expect crash-restarts to persist until S4 lands — reasons now name them),
    hook/commit lines (expect single `commit failed (...)` + FAILED, no
    restart storm).
4.4 Record confounds: backend build number at AFTER time, which of S1/S2/S4/S6
    have deployed, and any deploys that restarted the backend in-window
    (Cause-6 upkeep: any `interrupted by server restart` row re-opens it).

Gate: `RECOUNT-AFTER.md` with the post-converge-gated verdict per S5 gate
(pass/fail + counts), plus the confound ledger.

## Phase 5 — Baseline record + handoff (closes the task)

5.1 Write `BASELINE.md`: the new S1–S4 reference — BEFORE/AFTER §2 tables,
    per-runner versions + converge timestamps, backend builds, window dates,
    E5 verdicts, open evidence gaps, and the exact re-run commands (Phase 0 kit).
5.2 Handoff notes: unblock prod CONFIRMATION of S3/S4/S2-runner-half (code work
    never waited); S1/S6 confirm against `BASELINE.md` + their own deploys.
    If 2.4 triggered, link the new Cause-5 ticket; otherwise state explicitly
    that no new Cause-5 code is needed.
5.3 Review-checklist pass (RESPONSE.md): no PROD command ran without permission;
    exhibit worktrees untouched; recount recorded before any victory claim.

Gate: `BASELINE.md` present and self-contained — a stranger can re-run the
whole proof from the kit + this file alone.

## Validation & assurance plan (how we know it worked)

No unit tests by design (ops task — RESPONSE.md S5: "No new unit tests;
deliverable is the recount + version record"). Assurance instead comes from
executed procedures with saved evidence, each claim cross-checked two ways:

| Claim | Primary evidence | Independent cross-check |
|---|---|---|
| Runners on fix build | `GET /runners` version facts | `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0` + heartbeat build fields |
| Bare → ~0 | Fleet script `bare` count post-converge | Reason-vocabulary audit (1.3): every new interrupt carries a reason naming a cause |
| No commit crash-loops | FAILED + `gitFailure` completions, no interrupt row | Journal: single `commit failed` per incident, no restart storm |
| E5 classification | Worktree stage-output-commit presence | Journal `Runner failed:` line + origin SHA check |
| No server-restart orphans | `server_restart` count stays 0 | Backend build/`engine.updatedAt` divergence log (Cause-6 upkeep) |

Per-phase gates above double as the test plan: a phase is done only when its
artifact file exists with the named content. Negative controls: (a) BEFORE
snapshot must show still-bare new interrupts (proves the premise that 0.1.0
emits no reasons); (b) any reasoned non-cap interrupt pre-converge, or any
bare interrupt post-converge, fails its gate and must be explained, not
averaged away. Docs assurance: every record file carries timestamps, raw
command output (or the raw JSON), and the exact re-run command.

## Deliverables (all under `docs/tasks/683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c/`)

- `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` (this file) · `SURVEY.md` (prior stage, read-only
  input) · `RUN-LOG.md` · `bin/fleet-recount.sh` · `bin/runners-snapshot.sh` ·
  `bin/e5-sweep.sh` · `runners-before/*.json` + `runners-after/*.json` ·
  `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md` · `RECOUNT-AFTER.md` · `E5-SWEEP.md` · `BASELINE.md`.

## Risks & non-goals

- Convergence may take >24 h per runner (daily nudge, idle-only). Mitigation:
  q3 default waits in-run; q3-fallback splits BEFORE/Phase 2 now, AFTER later.
- S1/S2/S4/S6 landing mid-window confounds attribution. Mitigation: confound
  ledger + per-runner converge-time gating (§Approach).
- E5 exhibits already thinning (all four seeds absent on server2-alpha).
  Mitigation: sweep early (Phase 2), sibling host + origin + journal fallbacks,
  explicit gap notes.
- Access refusal (q2-fallbacks). Mitigation: degraded-scope branches per survey
  row; procedure-only doc as last resort.
- Non-goals: no runner/backend code, no knob change under the default
  assumption, no restarts/updates/reaps/re-runs, no Cause-5 ticket unless 2.4
  triggers, no claiming S1/S2/S4/S6 signals as S5 wins.

## Open questions

1. SURVEY.md q1–q4 — **answered** (all recommended). q1's answer ("knob
   already set") is falsified by live data; q3's answer ("wait same-run")
   fell back to BEFORE-now/AFTER-later (table above + `RUN-LOG.md`).
2. RESPONSE_SURVEY.md q1–q9 unanswered, including q9 (rollout pace) — q9's
   recommended option is treated as a hard constraint regardless.
3. Live `runnerRecommendedVersion` value — read-only check in 0.3 decides
   whether the rollout is already switched on.
4. Whether any E5 seed worktree survives on the local-alpha host — answered by
   the first sweep in Phase 2.
5. q4-fallback needs the full project list if "all projects" is chosen —
   enumerate via `GET /tasks` without project filter at that point.

## Sources (all inspected in-branch or in-checkout this run)

- `kb/2e663986` branch: `RESPONSE.md` (S5 + blocking map + checklist),
  `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` (§2 table, Causes 1–6, amplifier, E1–E7 matrix, §6
  method), `GUIDE-05-commit-push-crash-loop.md` (§4 E5 sweep),

backend API + runner journals + worktree reads on both hosts).

## Method

   runner interrupts across 20 tasks, from the frozen-kit BEFORE recount

# REVIEW — S5 stage review of `kb/683f0bfd` work products (PR-review stage, docs-only)

Task: `683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c` (RESPONSE.md S5 of `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4`).
Reviewer: review stage, 2026-11-23T10:46:33Z. Read-only against prod (GET /runners, GET /deploy/status,
GET /tasks fixtures already on disk); no runner/backend writes, no restarts, no reaps (q9 held).
Sources re-read: `RESPONSE.md` S5, `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` §2 + Cause 5, `GUIDE-05` §4,
`GUIDE-07` §5, `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q9, `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`, this folder's
`IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` / `SURVEY.md` / `bin/` / `raw/` / `runners-before/` / `recount-before-*`,
and the repo code/git (`runner-v0.2.0` tag, `046a6391`, `7ac148ce`, `api/config/schema.js`,
`api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js`).

## Verdict summary

**FAIL — needs more work before integrate.** The observe-only BEFORE evidence is good and the
premise still holds (0.1.0 runners emit no non-cap reasons), but (a) the task's central premise
is falsified: the only published 0.2.x release, tag `runner-v0.2.0`, does **not** contain the
fix `046a6391`, and the live backend still recommends `0.1.0`, so no runner can converge to a
fix-bearing build in the current state; (b) the test suite that is supposed to pin the ops kit
is broken and never reaches its e2e tests; (c) the plan's named deliverables are missing and one
evidence sweep (server2) is an unexplained empty file.

## Review questions

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Achieves the goal (converge runners to a build with `046a6391` + before/after recount)? | **No.** Only the BEFORE half exists (`runners-after/` empty). Convergence is currently impossible — see F1/F2. |
| Followed the plan? | Partially: Phase 0–2 executed (kit, before snapshot, before recount, local E5 sweep). Phases 3–5 not done; plan deliverables `RUN-LOG.md`, `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md`, `E5-SWEEP.md`, `BASELINE.md` absent. Survey q1 answer ("knob already set") is contradicted by live data and never reconciled. |
| Code standards? | Ops scripts: yes (fail-loud, atomic writes, validated task ids, read-only probes, no secrets). Test suite: **no** — F3. |
| Easy to modify later? | Yes — modular `bin/jq/*`, env overrides, mock API. |
| Best practices? | Mostly; E5 classification grep is not task-scoped (F5); empty server2 sweep has no gap note (F4). |
| Unnecessary tech debt? | Minor: two e5 worklist files in different shapes; before artifacts produced by an older script revision (no `recount-before-meta.json`/`-errors.jsonl`). |
| Docs updated? | `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` + `SURVEY.md` present, but the plan's "grounded facts" are wrong (F1/F2) and the narrative records are missing (F4). |

## Findings

### F1 (blocker — premise falsified) — `runner-v0.2.0` does NOT contain the fix

- `git rev-parse runner-v0.2.0^{commit}` → `8460e4a83f6664bcdd353b7307cfd03da7149d6f`, dated
  **2026-11-19 22:47:45Z**. The fix `046a6391` was merged **2026-11-21 09:38:57Z** in `7ac148ce`.
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0^{commit}` → **rc=1 (NO)** — the plan's own
  success criterion 1 check fails.
- `git show runner-v0.2.0:shared/gitFailure.js` → "exists on disk, but not in runner-v0.2.0";
  the generic catch in `runner-v0.2.0:runner/daemon.js` attaches **no** interrupt reason
  (only the workdir-cap path does). At HEAD the generic catch sends `interruptReason` and the
  `gitFailure` branch exists (`runner/daemon.js:2366-2374`, `:2441-2447`).
- Consequence: the plan's grounded fact "release tags `runner-v0.1.0` AND `runner-v0.2.0` both
  exist, so the 0.2.x release is already cut (runbook step 4 done)" conflates tag existence with
  tag content. Converging runners to the published `0.2.0` would still leave them without
  reasons and without deterministic-git-failure handling — bare interrupts would persist.
- Required (PROD-ACTION, outside this docs-only task, record as blocking prerequisite): cut a
  **new** release (e.g. `runner-v0.2.1`) from a commit ≥ `7ac148ce` per runbook ("never move an
  existing tag"), then raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (runbook step 5).

### F2 (blocker — live rollout state) — knob still 0.1.0, no nudge pending

Read-only `GET http://192.168.1.206:3100/runners` at **2026-11-23T10:36:57Z** (saved as
`runners-review/runners-20261123T103657Z.{json,tsv}`):

- All active runners (`local-alpha`, `local-bravo`, `server2-alpha`) report `runnerVersion 0.1.0`;
  `recommendedVersion 0.1.0`; `availableVersions ["0.1.0"]`; `updateAvailable false`;
  `pendingCommands []` — **no update nudge is even pending**.
- `availableVersions` = runner-reported versions + recommended/minimum knobs only
  (`api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js:224-244` `fleetKnownVersions`), so `["0.1.0"]` confirms the
  live `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` is still `0.1.0` (`api/config/schema.js:425-432`
  default). This contradicts `SURVEY.md` q1's answer ("already set — observe only"); no record
  in the folder reconciles the two.
- `local-alpha`/`local-bravo` build sha `fbcf8442ee031e2edbc9f0b30195afa410296cf3`
  (built 2026-11-14): `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 fbcf8442…` → **NO**.
  `server2-alpha` reports **no build sha** — by design the snapshot verdict must say
  "cannot verify", never converged.
- Backend build: `GET /deploy/status` → build 637, deployed 2026-11-21T22:00:17Z,
  headSha `7ac148ce…` (backend has the fix; runners don't).
- Consequence: q3's "wait until both converge, then after-recount in the same run" cannot
  complete in this state. The task must either wait on F1's prerequisite (human PROD-ACTION) or
  switch to the q3-fallback (deliver BEFORE + E5 now, AFTER as a scheduled follow-up) — and say
  so explicitly in `RUN-LOG.md`.

### F3 (verification broken) — `bin/tests/run-tests.sh` does not pass as committed

Re-ran the suite at ~2026-11-23T10:40Z (log captured in the session; nothing written outside
`$WORK` temp):

- T1–T5, T7, T8 **pass** (incl. T1: current `jq/per-task.jq` + `jq/aggregate.jq` over all 81
  `raw/before/*.json` fixtures reproduce `recount-before-table.json` exactly, and T6 ancestry:
  HEAD contains fix → true, `runner-v0.2.0` lacks fix → false).
- **T6 verdict checks FAIL ×4**: `mk_runner()` (run-tests.sh ~line 132) has an extra closing
  brace — `…build: (if $sha == "" then null else {sha: $sha} end)}}}}` → jq 1.8.1 syntax error
  at column 194 — so all four `runner-verdict.jq` assertions receive empty input and FAIL.
- Suite then **aborts at line 191**: `MOCK_BADJSON_ID: unbound variable` — `VAR=… start_mock …`
  prefix assignments do not persist after the function call under bash 5.3 + `set -u`, so the
  next line's `$MOCK_BADJSON_ID` is unbound; `set -e` kills the script. **T9-badjson, T10
  (fleet-recount e2e), T11 (runners-snapshot e2e), T12 never execute and no `RESULT:` line is
  printed.** The header comment's claim "pinned by bin/tests/run-tests.sh" is therefore
  unproven for everything past T9, and no test-result artifact is stored in the folder.

### F4 (deliverables / evidence gaps)

- `runners-after/` is empty; `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md`, `E5-SWEEP.md`, `RUN-LOG.md`, `BASELINE.md`
  (named in the plan's Deliverables) do not exist — only raw artifacts.
- `raw/e5-sweep-server2-before.txt` is **0 bytes** with no evidence-gap note. The server2 host
  is where the 413/502 journal evidence lives (WIDE_NET Cause 2/4); the local-only sweep
  cannot substitute for it. Record the gap explicitly or re-run when server2 ssh works.
- `recount-before-meta.json` / `recount-before-errors.jsonl` absent — the before artifacts were
  produced by an earlier script revision (`raw/recount-before-stderr.txt` format ≠ current
  `fleet-recount.sh` log format). T1 passing mitigates this for the numbers; still, re-run the
  before with the frozen kit (or note why not).
- `raw/e5-worklist-before.json` (flat `{task,ts,runner,delta}` rows) differs in shape from
  `recount-before-e5worklist.json` (grouped by task, 19 entries) — duplicate worklists, no note
  which is canonical.
- `runners-before/` has no `verdict-*.txt/json` — `runners-snapshot.sh` writes them, so the
  before snapshot predates the verdict feature.

### F5 (minor, classification accuracy) — e5-sweep stage-output grep is not task-scoped

`bin/e5-sweep.sh` detects a stage-output commit via `git log --format=%s -20 … | grep -qi
"stage output"` without matching the task's own branch. On mirror/merged history the last 20
subjects can belong to other tasks — observed in `raw/e5-sweep-before.txt`, where the origin
listing under `kb/7f6220c3-…` shows `kb/1cae113f-…` stage-output commits. A false "PRESENT"
would flip a verdict to Cause 2/4. Fix: match `^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output` (or check the ref tip).

### F6 (positives — what holds)

- Observe-only discipline held throughout: no restarts/updates/reaps/re-runs; all prod access
  was read-only GETs (q2/q9).
- Negative control holds: `recount-before-table.json` (81 tasks, project

# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — S5: Roll out 0.2.x runners and run fleet before/after interrupt recount

Task: `683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c` (RESPONSE.md S5 of `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4`).
Type: ops + verification. No code changes, no new unit tests.
Date: 2026-11-23. Status: BEFORE + E5 delivered under the q3-fallback
(see `RUN-LOG.md`, `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md`, `E5-SWEEP.md`, `BASELINE.md`);
the AFTER recount is a scheduled follow-up gated on a human PROD-ACTION
(raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the fix-bearing release).

## Goal

Confirm both production runners (`local-alpha`, `server2-alpha`) converge via the
normal idle-update channel to a build containing the deterministic-git-failure fix
(`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in `7ac148ce`), then prove with fleet-wide
before/after counts that the 0.2.x rollout resolves the "bare interrupt" class:
bare interrupts drop to ~0, reasons name Causes 1/3/4, and deterministic commit
failures surface as FAILED completions with `gitFailure` payloads instead of
interrupts. Record the post-rollout counts as the new baseline for S1–S4.

## Success criteria

1. `GET /runners` versions recorded before AND after; both named runners observed
   on a `0.2.x` build whose release contains `046a6391` (verified via
   `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0`, not by version string alone).
2. WIDE_NET §2 counts + GUIDE-07 §5 fleet script re-run on the same scope,
   recorded in the task folder as before/after tables.
3. S5-attributable signals move as predicted: bare interrupts → ~0 on new
   interrupts, `with_reason` names Causes 1/3/4, deterministic commit failures
   appear as FAILED + `gitFailure` (never interrupts). (Cap-escalation and label
   fixes are S1/S6 territory — see §"Attribution boundaries".)
4. E5 forensics sweep (GUIDE-05 §4) executed for every remaining post-`finished`
   interrupt: each classified commit-present (Cause 2/4) or commit-absent
   (Cause 5 suspect), with evidence or an explicit evidence-gap note.
5. Post-rollout baseline recorded in the task folder and usable by S1–S4 as their
   "before" reference (counts + runner versions + backend build + window dates).
6. Zero forced restarts, zero reaped exhibit worktrees, zero agent re-runs:
   observe-only throughout (q9 constraint).

No unit tests by design (ops task — RESPONSE.md S5: "No new unit tests;
deliverable is the recount + version record"). Assurance instead comes from
executed procedures with saved evidence, each claim cross-checked two ways:

| Claim | Primary evidence | Independent cross-check |
|---|---|---|
| Runners on fix build | `GET /runners` version facts | `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0` + heartbeat build fields |

snapshot must show still-bare new interrupts (proves the premise that 0.1.0
emits no reasons); (b) any reasoned non-cap interrupt pre-converge, or any
bare interrupt post-converge, fails its gate and must be explained, not

## Approach — make observation easy, then observe

This task changes nothing; its failure mode is fuzzy, non-reproducible numbers.
So Phase 0 ("make change easy") builds all reusable observation tooling first —
frozen scripts, record templates, access checks, and the BEFORE snapshot — and
only then do the time-ordered phases run. Big/volatile evidence comes early:
the BEFORE recount and the E5 sweep run before the convergence wait, because
interrupts keep accruing and worktree exhibits keep getting reaped (all four
E5 seed exhibits are already absent from this host). The long pole — idle
convergence at most daily per runner — waits in Phase 3 without blocking
Phase 1/2 evidence.

Attribution boundaries (what S5 may and may not claim): S1 (cap counting),
S2-backend (413 limit), S4 (transient tolerance), S6 (labels/counts) all change
the same signals. S5's after-recount MUST record the backend build number
(`GET /deploy/status`) and which sibling fixes have landed, and split new
interrupts by timestamp against each runner's converge time. Only interrupts
timestamped after a runner converged to 0.2.x count as "after" for S5.
`escalated` dropping is an S1 signal, not an S5 gate; the S5 gates are bare→~0,
reasons present, and FAILED+`gitFailure` instead of commit-loop interrupts.

## Validation & assurance plan (how we know it worked)

No unit tests by design (ops task — RESPONSE.md S5: "No new unit tests;
deliverable is the recount + version record"). Assurance instead comes from
executed procedures with saved evidence, each claim cross-checked two ways:

| Claim | Primary evidence | Independent cross-check |
|---|---|---|
| Runners on fix build | `GET /runners` version facts | `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0` + heartbeat build fields |
| Bare → ~0 | Fleet script `bare` count post-converge | Reason-vocabulary audit (1.3): every new interrupt carries a reason naming a cause |
| No commit crash-loops | FAILED + `gitFailure` completions, no interrupt row | Journal: single `commit failed` per incident, no restart storm |
| E5 classification | Worktree stage-output-commit presence | Journal `Runner failed:` line + origin SHA check |
| No server-restart orphans | `server_restart` count stays 0 | Backend build/`engine.updatedAt` divergence log (Cause-6 upkeep) |

Per-phase gates above double as the test plan: a phase is done only when its
artifact file exists with the named content. Negative controls: (a) BEFORE
snapshot must show still-bare new interrupts (proves the premise that 0.1.0
emits no reasons); (b) any reasoned non-cap interrupt pre-converge, or any
bare interrupt post-converge, fails its gate and must be explained, not
averaged away. Docs assurance: every record file carries timestamps, raw
command output (or the raw JSON), and the exact re-run command.

Task: `683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c` (RESPONSE.md S5 of `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4`).
Type: ops + verification. No code changes, no new unit tests.
Date: 2026-11-23. Status: BEFORE + E5 delivered under the q3-fallback
(see `RUN-LOG.md`, `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md`, `E5-SWEEP.md`, `BASELINE.md`);
the AFTER recount is a scheduled follow-up gated on a human PROD-ACTION
(raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the fix-bearing release).

## Goal

Confirm both production runners (`local-alpha`, `server2-alpha`) converge via the
normal idle-update channel to a build containing the deterministic-git-failure fix
(`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in `7ac148ce`), then prove with fleet-wide
before/after counts that the 0.2.x rollout resolves the "bare interrupt" class:
bare interrupts drop to ~0, reasons name Causes 1/3/4, and deterministic commit
failures surface as FAILED completions with `gitFailure` payloads instead of
interrupts. Record the post-rollout counts as the new baseline for S1–S4.

## Success criteria

1. `GET /runners` versions recorded before AND after; both named runners observed
   on a `0.2.x` build whose release contains `046a6391` (verified via
   `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0`, not by version string alone).
2. WIDE_NET §2 counts + GUIDE-07 §5 fleet script re-run on the same scope,
   recorded in the task folder as before/after tables.
3. S5-attributable signals move as predicted: bare interrupts → ~0 on new
   interrupts, `with_reason` names Causes 1/3/4, deterministic commit failures
   appear as FAILED + `gitFailure` (never interrupts). (Cap-escalation and label
   fixes are S1/S6 territory — see §"Attribution boundaries".)
4. E5 forensics sweep (GUIDE-05 §4) executed for every remaining post-`finished`
   interrupt: each classified commit-present (Cause 2/4) or commit-absent
   (Cause 5 suspect), with evidence or an explicit evidence-gap note.
5. Post-rollout baseline recorded in the task folder and usable by S1–S4 as their
   "before" reference (counts + runner versions + backend build + window dates).
6. Zero forced restarts, zero reaped exhibit worktrees, zero agent re-runs:
   observe-only throughout (q9 constraint).

## Approach — make observation easy, then observe

This task changes nothing; its failure mode is fuzzy, non-reproducible numbers.
So Phase 0 ("make change easy") builds all reusable observation tooling first —
frozen scripts, record templates, access checks, and the BEFORE snapshot — and
only then do the time-ordered phases run. Big/volatile evidence comes early:
the BEFORE recount and the E5 sweep run before the convergence wait, because
interrupts keep accruing and worktree exhibits keep getting reaped (all four
E5 seed exhibits are already absent from this host). The long pole — idle
convergence at most daily per runner — waits in Phase 3 without blocking
Phase 1/2 evidence.

Attribution boundaries (what S5 may and may not claim): S1 (cap counting),
S2-backend (413 limit), S4 (transient tolerance), S6 (labels/counts) all change
the same signals. S5's after-recount MUST record the backend build number
(`GET /deploy/status`) and which sibling fixes have landed, and split new
interrupts by timestamp against each runner's converge time. Only interrupts
timestamped after a runner converged to 0.2.x count as "after" for S5.
`escalated` dropping is an S1 signal, not an S5 gate; the S5 gates are bare→~0,
reasons present, and FAILED+`gitFailure` instead of commit-loop interrupts.

## Validation & assurance plan (how we know it worked)

No unit tests by design (ops task — RESPONSE.md S5: "No new unit tests;
deliverable is the recount + version record"). Assurance instead comes from
executed procedures with saved evidence, each claim cross-checked two ways:

| Claim | Primary evidence | Independent cross-check |
|---|---|---|
| Runners on fix build | `GET /runners` version facts | `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0` + heartbeat build fields |
| Bare → ~0 | Fleet script `bare` count post-converge | Reason-vocabulary audit (1.3): every new interrupt carries a reason naming a cause |
| No commit crash-loops | FAILED + `gitFailure` completions, no interrupt row | Journal: single `commit failed` per incident, no restart storm |
| E5 classification | Worktree stage-output-commit presence | Journal `Runner failed:` line + origin SHA check |
| No server-restart orphans | `server_restart` count stays 0 | Backend build/`engine.updatedAt` divergence log (Cause-6 upkeep) |

Per-phase gates above double as the test plan: a phase is done only when its
artifact file exists with the named content. Negative controls: (a) BEFORE
snapshot must show still-bare new interrupts (proves the premise that 0.1.0
emits no reasons); (b) any reasoned non-cap interrupt pre-converge, or any
bare interrupt post-converge, fails its gate and must be explained, not
averaged away. Docs assurance: every record file carries timestamps, raw
command output (or the raw JSON), and the exact re-run command.

# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — S5: Roll out 0.2.x runners and run fleet before/after interrupt recount

Task: `683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c` (RESPONSE.md S5 of `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4`).
Type: ops + verification. No code changes, no new unit tests.
Date: 2026-11-23. Status: BEFORE + E5 delivered under the q3-fallback
(see `RUN-LOG.md`, `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md`, `E5-SWEEP.md`, `BASELINE.md`);
the AFTER recount is a scheduled follow-up gated on a human PROD-ACTION
(raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the fix-bearing release).

## Goal

Confirm both production runners (`local-alpha`, `server2-alpha`) converge via the
normal idle-update channel to a build containing the deterministic-git-failure fix
(`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in `7ac148ce`), then prove with fleet-wide
before/after counts that the 0.2.x rollout resolves the "bare interrupt" class:
bare interrupts drop to ~0, reasons name Causes 1/3/4, and deterministic commit
failures surface as FAILED completions with `gitFailure` payloads instead of
interrupts. Record the post-rollout counts as the new baseline for S1–S4.

## Success criteria

1. `GET /runners` versions recorded before AND after; both named runners observed
   on a `0.2.x` build whose release contains `046a6391` (verified via
   `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0`, not by version string alone).
2. WIDE_NET §2 counts + GUIDE-07 §5 fleet script re-run on the same scope,
   recorded in the task folder as before/after tables.
3. S5-attributable signals move as predicted: bare interrupts → ~0 on new
   interrupts, `with_reason` names Causes 1/3/4, deterministic commit failures
   appear as FAILED + `gitFailure` (never interrupts). (Cap-escalation and label
   fixes are S1/S6 territory — see §"Attribution boundaries".)
4. E5 forensics sweep (GUIDE-05 §4) executed for every remaining post-`finished`
   interrupt: each classified commit-present (Cause 2/4) or commit-absent
   (Cause 5 suspect), with evidence or an explicit evidence-gap note.
5. Post-rollout baseline recorded in the task folder and usable by S1–S4 as their
   "before" reference (counts + runner versions + backend build + window dates).
6. Zero forced restarts, zero reaped exhibit worktrees, zero agent re-runs:
   observe-only throughout (q9 constraint).

## Approach — make observation easy, then observe

This task changes nothing; its failure mode is fuzzy, non-reproducible numbers.
So Phase 0 ("make change easy") builds all reusable observation tooling first —
frozen scripts, record templates, access checks, and the BEFORE snapshot — and
only then do the time-ordered phases run. Big/volatile evidence comes early:
the BEFORE recount and the E5 sweep run before the convergence wait, because
interrupts keep accruing and worktree exhibits keep getting reaped (all four
E5 seed exhibits are already absent from this host). The long pole — idle
convergence at most daily per runner — waits in Phase 3 without blocking
Phase 1/2 evidence.

Attribution boundaries (what S5 may and may not claim): S1 (cap counting),
S2-backend (413 limit), S4 (transient tolerance), S6 (labels/counts) all change
the same signals. S5's after-recount MUST record the backend build number
(`GET /deploy/status`) and which sibling fixes have landed, and split new
interrupts by timestamp against each runner's converge time. Only interrupts
timestamped after a runner converged to 0.2.x count as "after" for S5.
`escalated` dropping is an S1 signal, not an S5 gate; the S5 gates are bare→~0,
reasons present, and FAILED+`gitFailure` instead of commit-loop interrupts.

## Phase 2 — E5 forensics sweep (early: exhibits are volatile)

For each post-`finished` interrupt from 1.2 (seeds: `158394ab`, `db49d6c6`,
`1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`, plus any new ones from 1.1):

2.1 Worktree check per host (read-only, never reap): resolve the runner work
    root on that host first, then
    `git -C $WORK_ROOT/kb-<taskId>* log --oneline -3` and look for a
    stage-output commit matching the execution window. Present → Cause 2/4
    territory; absent → Cause 5 suspect. Record exact SHAs or exact absence.
2.2 Journal join (same host, same window): `Runner failed:` line text +
    restart-counter deltas — names hook/commit vs 413 vs 502/fetch-fail.
2.3 Fallback chain when a worktree is absent (already the case on server2-alpha
    for all four seeds): (a) check the sibling host; (b) check `origin` for the
    stage-output SHA (pushed = commit succeeded, Cause 2/4); (c) journal line
    alone; (d) if all absent, record an explicit evidence gap — never guess.
2.4 Verdict per interrupt: Cause-2/4 vs Cause-5-covered-by-`046a6391` vs
    Cause-5-NOT-covered. The third verdict is the ONLY trigger for new code:
    if and only if E5 finds commit-loop cases `046a6391` does not cover
    (a deterministic failure class outside `HOOK_REJECTED`/`COMMIT_FAILED`/
    `MERGE_CONFLICT` that still crash-loops on 0.2.x), file a NEW Cause-5
    code ticket with the journal line + worktree state + failing class.

Gate: `E5-SWEEP.md` with one row per post-`finished` interrupt (evidence or
gap) + the ticket/no-ticket decision with reasoning.

## Phase 3 — Convergence watch (the long pole; observe only)

3.1 Poll `GET /runners` on a slow cadence (30–60 min) and snapshot each poll.
    Per runner record: running version + build facts, `updateAvailable` /
    `belowMinimum` / `updateStatus` badges, pending vs acked `requestUpdate`
    (nudge cooldown is 24 h), busy/idle, pinned-vs-Latest.
3.2 Declare a runner converged at the first poll showing a 0.2.x build whose
    release contains `046a6391`; record the converge timestamp per runner in
    `RUN-LOG.md`. Both converged → proceed to Phase 4 (q3 default).
3.3 If a runner stalls (badge never clears past 24–48 h): triage READ-ONLY per
    the runbook ("a runner says out of date") — `entrypoint: direct` vs
    wrapper, `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` opt-out, pinned version, pin
    older than running, recommended knob above every release, `updateStatus`
    failure reason — and record the blocking cause. Fixes (migrate, flip the
    switch, Update button) are PROD-ACTION: propose, do not perform.
3.4 NEVER to speed convergence: force-restart mid-assignment, Update-on-busy,
    reaping worktrees, re-running parked tasks. Any of these manufactures the
    interrupts being measured (q9 / PROD-ACTION ban).

Gate: per-runner converge timestamps, or a stalled-runner triage note with a
named blocking cause. Under the q3-fallback (before-now/stop), Phase 3 becomes
a scheduled follow-up run instead of a same-run wait.

## Validation & assurance plan (how we know it worked)

No unit tests by design (ops task — RESPONSE.md S5: "No new unit tests;
deliverable is the recount + version record"). Assurance instead comes from
executed procedures with saved evidence, each claim cross-checked two ways:

| Claim | Primary evidence | Independent cross-check |
|---|---|---|
| Runners on fix build | `GET /runners` version facts | `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0` + heartbeat build fields |
| Bare → ~0 | Fleet script `bare` count post-converge | Reason-vocabulary audit (1.3): every new interrupt carries a reason naming a cause |
| No commit crash-loops | FAILED + `gitFailure` completions, no interrupt row | Journal: single `commit failed` per incident, no restart storm |
| E5 classification | Worktree stage-output-commit presence | Journal `Runner failed:` line + origin SHA check |
| No server-restart orphans | `server_restart` count stays 0 | Backend build/`engine.updatedAt` divergence log (Cause-6 upkeep) |

Per-phase gates above double as the test plan: a phase is done only when its
artifact file exists with the named content. Negative controls: (a) BEFORE
snapshot must show still-bare new interrupts (proves the premise that 0.1.0
emits no reasons); (b) any reasoned non-cap interrupt pre-converge, or any
bare interrupt post-converge, fails its gate and must be explained, not
averaged away. Docs assurance: every record file carries timestamps, raw
command output (or the raw JSON), and the exact re-run command.

1|#!/usr/bin/env bash
2|# runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — record the fleet matrix
3|# (GET /runners + GET /deploy/status) and a per-runner convergence verdict.
4|# READ-ONLY against the backend; safe to run any time, any number of times.
5|#
6|# Outputs in <outdir>:
7|#   runners-<stamp>.json        raw GET /runners payload (evidence)
8|#   runners-<stamp>.tsv         flat fleet table incl. build sha/builtAt
9|#   deploy-status-<stamp>.json  raw GET /deploy/status payload
10|#   verdict-<stamp>.txt         one line per named runner: CONVERGED or the reasons why not

35|  local sha="$1" repo_root="$2" fix_commit="$3"
36|  if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ "$sha" = "null" ]; then
37|    echo null
38|    return 0
39|  fi
40|  if ! git -C "$repo_root" cat-file -e "$sha^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
41|    echo null
42|    return 0
43|  fi
44|  if git -C "$repo_root" merge-base --is-ancestor "$fix_commit" "$sha" 2>/dev/null; then
45|    echo true
46|  else
47|    echo false
48|  fi
49|}
50|
51|# verdict_for <runners.json> <runnerId> — prints the verdict JSON object for one
52|# runner (jq/runner-verdict.jq + the git ancestry check).
53|verdict_for() {
54|  local runners_json="$1" runner_id="$2" repo_root="$3" fix_commit="$4"
55|  local runner sha fix
56|  runner="$(jq -c --arg id "$runner_id" '.[] | select(.runnerId == $id) // empty' "$runners_json")"
57|  if [ -z "$runner" ]; then
58|    printf '{"runnerId":"%s","converged":false,"reasons":["runner not present in GET /runners (offline/revoked?)"]}\n' "$runner_id"
59|    return 0
60|  fi
61|  sha="$(printf '%s' "$runner" | jq -r '.facts.versions.build.sha // ""')"
62|  fix="$(fix_in_build "$sha" "$repo_root" "$fix_commit")"
63|  jq -n -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/runner-verdict.jq" --argjson runner "$runner" --argjson fixInBuild "$fix"
64|}
65|
66|main() {
67|  require_commands curl jq git date mktemp
68|  local outdir="${1:-}"
69|  [ -n "$outdir" ] || die "usage: runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged]"
70|  local require_converged=0
71|  if [ "${2:-}" = "--require-converged" ]; then require_converged=1; fi
72|
73|  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
74|  local named="${KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS:-local-alpha,server2-alpha}"
75|  local fix_commit="${KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT:-046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4}"
76|  local task_dir repo_root stamp
77|  task_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
78|  repo_root="$(git -C "$task_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
79|  stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
80|  mkdir -p "$outdir"
81|
82|  log "runners-snapshot api=$api_base outdir=$outdir named=$named fix=$fix_commit"
83|
84|  local runners_json="$outdir/runners-$stamp.json" deploy_json="$outdir/deploy-status-$stamp.json"
85|  api_get_json "$api_base/runners" "$runners_json" \
86|    || die "GET $api_base/runners failed — nothing written to $outdir"
87|  api_get_json "$api_base/deploy/status" "$deploy_json" \
88|    || { log "WARN: GET /deploy/status failed — continuing with /runners only"; rm -f "$deploy_json"; }
89|
90|  jq -r -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/runners-tsv.jq" "$runners_json" > "$outdir/runners-$stamp.tsv"
91|
92|  local verdict_json="$outdir/verdict-$stamp.json" verdict_txt="$outdir/verdict-$stamp.txt"
93|  : > "$verdict_json.tmp"
94|  local IFS=',' r all_converged=1 v
95|  for r in $named; do
96|    v="$(verdict_for "$runners_json" "$r" "$repo_root" "$fix_commit")"
97|    printf '%s\n' "$v" >> "$verdict_json.tmp"
98|    if printf '%s' "$v" | jq -e '.converged == true' >/dev/null; then
99|      printf 'CONVERGED    %s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$v" | jq -r '[.runnerId, .runnerVersion, (.buildSha // "no-sha")] | join(" ")')" >> "$verdict_txt"
100|    else
101|      all_converged=0
102|      printf 'NOT-CONVERGED %s — %s\n' "$r" "$(printf '%s' "$v" | jq -r '.reasons | join("; ")')" >> "$verdict_txt"
103|    fi
104|  done
105|  jq -s '.' "$verdict_json.tmp" > "$verdict_json" && rm -f "$verdict_json.tmp"
106|
107|  {
108|    echo "# runner convergence verdict — $(date -u +%FT%TZ) — fix commit $fix_commit"
109|    echo "# converged = runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND running build sha contains the fix commit"
110|    cat "$verdict_txt"
111|  } > "$verdict_txt.hdr" && mv "$verdict_txt.hdr" "$verdict_txt"
112|
113|  echo "wrote $outdir/runners-$stamp.{json,tsv} ${deploy_json:+deploy-status-$stamp.json} verdict-$stamp.{json,txt}"
114|  cat "$outdir/runners-$stamp.tsv"
115|  echo "--- verdict:"
116|  cat "$verdict_txt"
117|
118|  if [ "$require_converged" = 1 ] && [ "$all_converged" = 0 ]; then
119|    log "--require-converged: not all named runners converged (see $verdict_txt)"
120|    exit 3
121|  fi
122|}
123|
124|if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
125|  main "$@"
126|fi

# Runner update runbook

Operator procedures for the runner self-update channel (Option A,
`docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md`): cutting releases,
rolling back, migrating hosts to the wrapper, and triaging a runner
that says out of date. The backend directs version selection but never
serves runner bytes (R05) — every procedure below preserves that.

## Cutting a runner release (normal path)

The tag is the version source of truth; the pipeline cuts it.

1. Bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json` (plain semver for
   fleet releases, e.g. `0.2.0`; suffixed tags like `0.3.0-rc.1` for
   canaries — v1 runners skip pre-releases automatically).
2. If the release needs a newer backend API, update the
   `requires.backendApi` range in the same file (e.g.
   `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`). The release builder refuses manifests without a
   compat claim, and runners filter on this range.
3. Merge to the main line through the normal review flow.
4. Publish the runner (`publish.sh` with the runner component). The
   publish cuts and pushes the annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which
   triggers `runner-release.yml`: full update-channel test gate, four
   platform archives, signed `manifest.json` + `.minisig`, GitHub
   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).
5. Raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the new version on
   the backend. That is the one managed place: trailers light the
   "update available" badge and the backend auto-nudges command-capable
   ones (`requestUpdate`, at most daily per runner). Runners converge
   on idle with no SSH. Leave `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` alone
   unless this is a breaking release (the 409 floor stops dispatch).

## Cutting a runner release (emergency path)

When the pipeline cannot cut the tag (CI down, urgent patch), tag by
hand from the release commit — the same builder runs:

```
git tag -a runner-vX.Y.Z -m "Runner runner-vX.Y.Z" <full-sha>
git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z
```

Then follow step 5 above. Never move an existing tag: cut a patch
version forward instead.

## Rollback drill (bad release, no host access needed)

1. Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release so `releases/latest`
   resolves to the prior tag.
2. Lower `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (and
   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` if it was raised past the bad
   version) to stop badge nagging and 409 loops.
3. Cut a patch release forward (normal path above). The updater never
   downgrades: runners still on older versions pick the prior release
   up on their next idle check, while runners already on the bad
   release stay there until the patch supersedes it.
4. Two automatic outs: a release that crashes on boot rolls itself
   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
   is cut.

Drill timing to record: un-publish → badges clear, patch cut →
fleet converged.

## Migrating a host to the wrapper

Direct `node main.js` units re-exec the same old directory on every
restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at
the stable wrapper shim — onto the SAME version (no update is staged,
so the fleet version does not change).

Per host, idle runners first; drain busy runners, then migrate:

```
# 1. Pre-check (read-only, safe any time):
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT=$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install \
  /path/to/runner/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service

# Runner update runbook

Operator procedures for the runner self-update channel (Option A,
`docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md`): cutting releases,
rolling back, migrating hosts to the wrapper, and triaging a runner
that says out of date. The backend directs version selection but never
serves runner bytes (R05) — every procedure below preserves that.

## Cutting a runner release (normal path)

The tag is the version source of truth; the pipeline cuts it.

1. Bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json` (plain semver for
   fleet releases, e.g. `0.2.0`; suffixed tags like `0.3.0-rc.1` for
   canaries — v1 runners skip pre-releases automatically).
2. If the release needs a newer backend API, update the
   `requires.backendApi` range in the same file (e.g.
   `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`). The release builder refuses manifests without a
   compat claim, and runners filter on this range.
3. Merge to the main line through the normal review flow.
4. Publish the runner (`publish.sh` with the runner component). The
   publish cuts and pushes the annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which
   triggers `runner-release.yml`: full update-channel test gate, four
   platform archives, signed `manifest.json` + `.minisig`, GitHub
   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).
5. Raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the new version on
   the backend. That is the one managed place: trailers light the
   "update available" badge and the backend auto-nudges command-capable
   ones (`requestUpdate`, at most daily per runner). Runners converge
   on idle with no SSH. Leave `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` alone
   unless this is a breaking release (the 409 floor stops dispatch).

## Cutting a runner release (emergency path)

When the pipeline cannot cut the tag (CI down, urgent patch), tag by
hand from the release commit — the same builder runs:

```
git tag -a runner-vX.Y.Z -m "Runner runner-vX.Y.Z" <full-sha>
git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z
```

Then follow step 5 above. Never move an existing tag: cut a patch
version forward instead.

## Rollback drill (bad release, no host access needed)

1. Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release so `releases/latest`
   resolves to the prior tag.
2. Lower `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (and
   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` if it was raised past the bad
   version) to stop badge nagging and 409 loops.
3. Cut a patch release forward (normal path above). The updater never
   downgrades: runners still on older versions pick the prior release
   up on their next idle check, while runners already on the bad
   release stay there until the patch supersedes it.
4. Two automatic outs: a release that crashes on boot rolls itself
   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
   is cut.

Drill timing to record: un-publish → badges clear, patch cut →
fleet converged.

## Migrating a host to the wrapper

Direct `node main.js` units re-exec the same old directory on every
restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at
the stable wrapper shim — onto the SAME version (no update is staged,
so the fleet version does not change).

Per host, idle runners first; drain busy runners, then migrate:

```
# 1. Pre-check (read-only, safe any time):
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT=$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install \
  /path/to/runner/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# fleet-recount.sh <label> [task-dir] — GUIDE-07 §5 fleet recount +
# WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table, over one project, read-only against the
# backend API (approved: this task's SURVEY.md q2). Scope is pinned to project
# 0fd41821-... so results compare directly with the 2026-11-21 baseline.
#
# Outputs (under task-dir, default: current directory):
#   raw/<label>/<taskId>.json        raw GET /tasks/<id> payloads (evidence)
#   recount-<label>.jsonl            one aggregated row per task  (jq/per-task.jq)
#   recount-<label>-table.json       WIDE_NET §2 aggregate         (jq/aggregate.jq)
#   recount-<label>-e5worklist.json  post-finished interrupts      (jq/e5-worklist.jq, GUIDE-05 §4 scope)
#   recount-<label>-errors.jsonl     tasks that failed to fetch/parse (only written on failure)
#   recount-<label>-meta.json        run metadata (api, project, window, counts)
#   stdout                           the §2 table + E5 worklist, for the run log
#
# Failure behaviour (deliberate, so a partial run is loud, never silent):
#   - the task list itself unreachable/invalid/empty -> exit 1, no outputs written
#   - one task fails to download or parse -> recorded in -errors.jsonl, the
#     loop continues, the table is still written, and the script exits 2 at
#     the end so the gap cannot be missed
#   - API base / project overridable via KAINBAIN_API_BASE / KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID
#     (the test suite drives this script against a local mock API)
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

main() {
  require_commands curl jq date mktemp
  local label="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$label" ] || die "usage: fleet-recount.sh <before|after|...> [task-dir]"
  local task_dir="${2:-$(pwd)}"
  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
  local project_id="${KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID:-0fd41821-d8a5-4e49-bc2e-28ce8c739a0a}"
  local raw_dir="$task_dir/raw/$label"
  mkdir -p "$raw_dir"
  local started; started="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  log "fleet-recount label=$label api=$api_base project=$project_id task_dir=$task_dir started=$started"

  # 1. task list — must be a non-empty array of well-formed ids, otherwise the
  #    API is down, the project id is wrong, or we got an error page.
  local list_tmp; list_tmp="$(mktemp)"
  if ! api_get_json "$api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id" "$list_tmp.list"; then
    rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
    die "cannot list tasks at $api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id — API down or wrong project; nothing written"
  fi
  local ids; ids="$(jq -r 'if type == "array" then (.[].id // empty) else empty end' "$list_tmp.list")"
  rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
  local n; n="$(printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -c . || true)"
  [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || die "GET /tasks returned zero tasks for project $project_id — refusing to write an empty baseline"
  if printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -qvE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'; then
    die "task list contains a malformed id — refusing to continue (got: $(printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -vE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' | head -3 | tr '\n' ' '))"
  fi
  log "task list ok: $n tasks"

  # 2. per-task fetch + aggregate row. One bad task never aborts the loop.
  local jsonl="$task_dir/recount-$label.jsonl" errors="$task_dir/recount-$label-errors.jsonl"
  local table="$task_dir/recount-$label-table.json" worklist="$task_dir/recount-$label-e5worklist.json"
  : > "$jsonl"
  : > "$errors"

31|  failed_stage: ([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("Stage failed in|Failed back to stage"))] | length),
32|  git_failure_streak: (($t.gitFailureStreak // {}).count // 0),
33|  last_error_git_kind: ((($t.lastError // {}).gitDiagnostics // {}).kind // null),
34|  interrupt_details: [

# server2-ssh.sh <remote command...> — run a command on the server2-alpha host

# printing, logging, or putting it on a command line (server2-ssh skill rules).
#
# Method: sshpass -f when installed (reads the file directly); otherwise a
# pexpect driver that opens the file inside Python and answers the prompt.
#
# Failure behaviour (this matters: a failed remote probe must not look like a
# success to the caller):
#   - no command given            -> usage on stderr, exit 64
#   - password file missing/empty  -> FATAL on stderr, exit 66 (contents never shown)
#   - password file not mode 600   -> warning on stderr (contents never shown)

#     the pexpect path reads child.exitstatus/signalstatus)
#
# Read-only usage only in this task (S5 observe-only, survey q9: never
# restart/update/reap anything on the runner hosts from here).

SSH_TARGET="server2@192.168.1.172"

  echo "usage: server2-ssh.sh '<remote command>'" >&2

if [ ! -f "$PASSWORD_FILE" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: password file $PASSWORD_FILE not found (expected mode 600, first line = password)" >&2
  exit 66

MODE="$(stat -c %a "$PASSWORD_FILE")"

  echo "WARN: $PASSWORD_FILE has mode $MODE, expected 600 — tighten it with: chmod 600 $PASSWORD_FILE" >&2
fi

if command -v sshpass >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # sshpass consumes the file itself; the password never enters argv or env.

  validate_task_prefix "$@"

  local task_dir repo_root work_root unit origin_repo since
  task_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
  repo_root="$(git -C "$task_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
  since="${E5_JOURNAL_SINCE:-2026-11-19}"

    work_root="${E5_WORK_ROOT:-/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work}"

    require_commands git

    unit="${E5_UNIT:-kainbain-runner-local-alpha}"
    origin_repo="${E5_ORIGIN_REPO:-$repo_root}"
    require_commands git
  fi

  echo "## E5 sweep host=$host work_root=$work_root unit=$unit origin_repo=$origin_repo since=$since at $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  local failed=0 t
  for t in "$@"; do
    if ! run_probe "$host" "$work_root" "$unit" "$origin_repo" "$t" "$since"; then
      failed=$((failed + 1))
      log "WARN: probe for kb-$t on $host failed — recorded, continuing with the next task"
      echo "VERDICT kb-$t: PROBE FAILED on $host (see stderr) — treat as evidence gap"
      echo
    fi
  done
  echo "## E5 sweep done: $# task(s), $failed probe failure(s) at $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
    log "exiting 2: $failed probe(s) failed"
    exit 2
  fi
}

Read text file `docs/KB Code Standards.md`.
1|# Values
2|
3|## User understandable over technical language
4|
5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible
6|
7|### Principles
8|
9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
12|- File structure should reflect the call stack
13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
14|- Include why things are done not just what is done
15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
18|- Every new export also carries a `MARK:` label in the same JSDoc block, sitting directly above the export (only whitespace between `*/` and `export`); `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s) checks this before pushing — copy-paste shapes in docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md §Documentation/Jsdoc
19|  
20|  
21|
22|## Functional over Object oreintated
23|
24|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).
25|
26|### Principles
27|
28|- Try and avoid using classes where possible
29|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
30|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
31|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
32|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
33|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
34|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility
35|
36|
37|## Co-location over abstraction
38|
39|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.
40|
41|### Principles
42|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
43|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
44|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
45|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
46|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
47|- Don’t fear repetition of code
48|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
49|- Use folders as a tool for organising
50|
51|## Tested over trusted 
52|
53|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 
54|
55|### Principles
56|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
57|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
58|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
59|- Tests must be consistent
60|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
61|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle
62|
63|
64|## Fast iteration over long planning
65|
66|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.
67|
68|### Principles
69|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
70|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
71|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
72|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
73|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
74|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.
75|
76|
77|
78|# Inspirations
79|My principles here are inspired by:
80|
81|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
82|- Life isn’t binary (book)
83|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)
84|
85|
86|# Examples
87|
88|## Intent Driven descriptions
89|
90|### Bad Example
91|
92|```js
93|
94|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {
95|
96|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}
97|
98|    users.push(user)
99|  
100|}
101|
102|const list = []
103|
104|userFactory("Frank",32,list)
105|
106|
107|```
108|
109|## Good example
110|
111|```js
112|
113|/**
114|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
115|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
116|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
117|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
118|*/
119|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
120|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
121|  
122|  return ageNextYear
123|}
124|
125|const userObjectsList = []
126|
127|const usersName = "Frank"
128|const usersAge = 32
129|
130|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})
131|
132|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})
133|
134|
135|```
