1|#!/usr/bin/env bash
2|# fleet-recount.sh <label> [task-dir] — GUIDE-07 §5 fleet recount +
3|# WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table, over one project, read-only against the
4|# backend API (approved: this task's SURVEY.md q2). Scope is pinned to project
5|# 0fd41821-... so results compare directly with the 2026-11-21 baseline.
6|#
7|# Outputs (under task-dir, default: current directory):
8|#   raw/<label>/<taskId>.json        raw GET /tasks/<id> payloads (evidence)
9|#   recount-<label>.jsonl            one aggregated row per task  (jq/per-task.jq)
10|#   recount-<label>-table.json       WIDE_NET §2 aggregate         (jq/aggregate.jq)
11|#   recount-<label>-e5worklist.json  post-finished interrupts      (jq/e5-worklist.jq, GUIDE-05 §4 scope)
12|#   recount-<label>-errors.jsonl     tasks that failed to fetch/parse (only written on failure)
13|#   recount-<label>-meta.json        run metadata (api, project, window, counts)
14|#   stdout                           the §2 table + E5 worklist, for the run log
15|#
16|# Failure behaviour (deliberate, so a partial run is loud, never silent):
17|#   - the task list itself unreachable/invalid/empty -> exit 1, no outputs written
18|#   - one task fails to download or parse -> recorded in -errors.jsonl, the
19|#     loop continues, the table is still written, and the script exits 2 at
20|#     the end so the gap cannot be missed
21|#   - API base / project overridable via KAINBAIN_API_BASE / KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID
22|#     (the test suite drives this script against a local mock API)
23|set -euo pipefail
24|SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
25|# shellcheck source=lib.sh
26|source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"
27|
28|main() {
29|  require_commands curl jq date mktemp
30|  local label="${1:-}"
31|  [ -n "$label" ] || die "usage: fleet-recount.sh <before|after|...> [task-dir]"
32|  local task_dir="${2:-$(pwd)}"
33|  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
34|  local project_id="${KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID:-0fd41821-d8a5-4e49-bc2e-28ce8c739a0a}"
35|  local raw_dir="$task_dir/raw/$label"
36|  mkdir -p "$raw_dir"
37|  local started; started="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
38|  log "fleet-recount label=$label api=$api_base project=$project_id task_dir=$task_dir started=$started"
39|
40|  # 1. task list — must be a non-empty array of well-formed ids, otherwise the
41|  #    API is down, the project id is wrong, or we got an error page.
42|  local list_tmp; list_tmp="$(mktemp)"
43|  if ! api_get_json "$api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id" "$list_tmp.list"; then
44|    rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
45|    die "cannot list tasks at $api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id — API down or wrong project; nothing written"
46|  fi
47|  local ids; ids="$(jq -r 'if type == "array" then (.[].id // empty) else empty end' "$list_tmp.list")"
48|  rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
49|  local n; n="$(printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -c . || true)"
50|  [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || die "GET /tasks returned zero tasks for project $project_id — refusing to write an empty baseline"
51|  if printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -qvE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'; then
52|    die "task list contains a malformed id — refusing to continue (got: $(printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -vE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' | head -3 | tr '\n' ' '))"
53|  fi
54|  log "task list ok: $n tasks"
55|
56|  # 2. per-task fetch + aggregate row. One bad task never aborts the loop.
57|  local jsonl="$task_dir/recount-$label.jsonl" errors="$task_dir/recount-$label-errors.jsonl"
58|  local table="$task_dir/recount-$label-table.json" worklist="$task_dir/recount-$label-e5worklist.json"
59|  : > "$jsonl"
60|  : > "$errors"
61|  local ok=0 failed=0 t raw row_tmp
62|  row_tmp="$(mktemp)"
63|  for t in $ids; do
64|    raw="$raw_dir/$t.json"
65|    if api_get_json "$api_base/tasks/$t?projectId=$project_id" "$raw" \
66|       && jq -e 'type == "object" and ((.history // []) | type == "array")' "$raw" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
67|       && jq -c -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/per-task.jq" "$raw" > "$row_tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
68|      cat "$row_tmp" >> "$jsonl"
69|      ok=$((ok + 1))
70|    else
71|      failed=$((failed + 1))
72|      rm -f "$raw"
73|      printf '{"task":"%s","error":"fetch or parse failed"}\n' "$t" >> "$errors"
74|      log "WARN: task $t failed to fetch/parse — recorded in recount-$label-errors.jsonl, continuing"
75|    fi
76|  done
77|  rm -f "$row_tmp"
78|  log "fetched $ok tasks, $failed failed"
79|
80|  # 3. aggregates (atomic writes), printed to stdout for the run log too.
81|  jq -s -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/aggregate.jq" "$jsonl" > "$table.tmp" && mv "$table.tmp" "$table"
82|  jq -s -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/e5-worklist.jq" "$jsonl" > "$worklist.tmp" && mv "$worklist.tmp" "$worklist"
83|  jq -n --arg label "$label" --arg api "$api_base" --arg project "$project_id" \
84|      --arg started "$started" --arg finished "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" \
85|      --argjson ok "$ok" --argjson failed "$failed" \
86|      '{label: $label, api: $api, project: $project, startedAt: $started, finishedAt: $finished, tasksFetched: $ok, tasksFailed: $failed}' \
87|    > "$task_dir/recount-$label-meta.json"
88|
89|  echo "## WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table — label=$label, project $project_id, $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
90|  jq . "$table"
91|  echo
92|  echo "## E5 worklist — post-finished interrupts (GUIDE-05 §4 scope), label=$label"
93|  jq . "$worklist"
94|  echo
95|  if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
96|    echo "## ERRORS — $failed task(s) failed, see recount-$label-errors.jsonl" >&2
97|    cat "$errors" >&2
98|    log "exiting 2: $failed of $n tasks failed"
99|    exit 2
100|  fi
101|  log "done: label=$label ok=$ok failed=$failed"
102|}
103|
104|if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
105|  main "$@"
106|fi

7|# pexpect driver that opens the file inside Python and answers the prompt.

10|# success to the caller):
11|#   - no command given            -> usage on stderr, exit 64
12|#   - password file missing/empty  -> FATAL on stderr, exit 66 (contents never shown)
13|#   - password file not mode 600   -> warning on stderr (contents never shown)
14|#   - connect/auth timeout         -> FATAL on stderr, partial output kept, exit 124
15|#   - otherwise the REMOTE exit code is propagated (ssh does this natively;
16|#     the pexpect path reads child.exitstatus/signalstatus)

18|# Read-only usage only in this task (S5 observe-only, survey q9: never
19|# restart/update/reap anything on the runner hosts from here).

28|  exit 64
29|fi

1|#!/usr/bin/env bash
2|# lib.sh — shared helpers for the S5 ops scripts in this folder (bin/).
3|# Sourced, never executed directly. Shared because every script here needs
4|# the same three things: loud logging, loud death, and a validated HTTP GET.
5|#
6|# Rule for this task folder: an ops evidence script must never silently
7|# degrade. Every helper below either succeeds completely or reports a clear
8|# error and returns non-zero, so a baseline built from these scripts is
9|# trustworthy.
10|
11|# log <message...> — timestamped progress line on stderr. stdout stays clean
12|# because the scripts print evidence tables (jsonl/tsv) on stdout.
13|log() {
14|  printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" >&2
15|}
16|
17|# die <message...> — report a clear, fatal setup/usage error and exit 1.
18|# Used where there is nothing to salvage (missing tool, unreachable API,
19|# bad arguments). Runtime per-item failures are handled by the callers
20|# (recorded, counted, non-zero exit at the end) — see fleet-recount.sh.
21|die() {
22|  log "FATAL: $*"
23|  exit 1
24|}
25|
26|# require_commands <cmd...> — fail before touching anything if a tool is
27|# missing, so the failure is about the environment, not about half-written
28|# evidence files.
29|require_commands() {
30|  local missing=() cmd
31|  for cmd in "$@"; do
32|    command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$cmd")
33|  done
34|  if [ "${#missing[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
35|    die "missing required commands: ${missing[*]} — install them or run on the runner host"
36|  fi
37|}
38|
39|# write_atomic <dest> <src-file> — copy src-file next to dest and rename over
40|# it, so a crashed run never leaves a half-written evidence file that looks
41|# complete. Same directory => the final mv is an atomic rename.
42|write_atomic() {
43|  local dest="$1" src="$2" tmp="$dest.tmp.$$"
44|  if ! cp "$src" "$tmp"; then
45|    rm -f "$tmp"
46|    log "ERROR: cannot write $dest"
47|    return 1
48|  fi
49|  mv "$tmp" "$dest"
50|}
51|
52|# api_get_json <url> <dest> — GET url into dest as validated JSON.
53|#   - retries transient network failures (curl --retry-connrefused)
54|#   - fails on any HTTP error status (curl -f, so a 500/404 body is NOT kept)
55|#   - refuses to store a 200 body that is not valid JSON (an HTML error page
56|#     must never end up in the evidence store)
57|#   - writes dest atomically
58|# Returns non-zero with a clear stderr line on any failure.
59|api_get_json() {
60|  local url="$1" dest="$2" tmp
61|  tmp="$(mktemp)"
62|  if ! curl -sfS -m 60 --retry 3 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 2 -o "$tmp" "$url"; then

64|    log "ERROR: GET $url failed (HTTP error or host unreachable after retries)"
65|    return 1
66|  fi
67|  if ! jq -e 'type == "object" or type == "array"' "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
68|    rm -f "$tmp"
69|    log "ERROR: GET $url returned a body that is not valid JSON — refusing to store it in $dest"
70|    return 1
71|  fi
72|  write_atomic "$dest" "$tmp"
73|  rm -f "$tmp"

77|# shell commands (locally and over ssh) by e5-sweep.sh, so they must be hex
78|# and dashes only. Accepts a short prefix (8 hex chars) or a full UUID.
79|# This is the injection guard for the sweep: anything else is rejected before
80|# any command runs.

11|#

13|# running build's reported git sha contains the fix commit — verified locally
14|# with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fixCommit> <buildSha>`, because a version
15|# string alone cannot prove which code is running. If the runner reports no
16|# build sha, the verdict says so instead of guessing.
17|#
18|# Knobs (env):
19|#   KAINBAIN_API_BASE            default http://192.168.1.206:3100
20|#   KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS    default "local-alpha,server2-alpha"

22|#

24|#   1 setup or API failure (nothing trustworthy written);
25|#   3 snapshot written, --require-converged given, but not all named runners converged.

32|# (no sha reported, or sha unknown to the local repo). Uses the local Kainbain
33|# checkout as the commit database — read-only git queries only.
34|fix_in_build() {

9|#     durable evidence that survives worktree reaping, with git log

1|#!/usr/bin/env python3
2|"""mock-api.py — a tiny local stand-in for the KainBain backend API, used ONLY
3|by bin/tests/run-tests.sh so the ops scripts can be integration-tested without
4|touching prod.
5|
6|Routes:
7|  GET /tasks?projectId=...   -> [{"id": <name>}, ...] for every <name>.json in
8|                                --tasks-dir ([] when MOCK_EMPTY=1)
9|  GET /tasks/<id>?projectId=... -> the contents of <id>.json (200);
10|                                500 when <id> is in MOCK_FAIL_IDS;
11|                                200 + invalid JSON when <id> == MOCK_BADJSON_ID
12|  GET /runners               -> contents of --runners-file (200)
13|  GET /deploy/status         -> contents of --deploy-file (200)
14|
15|--port 0 picks a free port and writes it to --port-file once listening.
16|"""
17|import argparse
18|import json
19|import os
20|import pathlib
21|from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
22|from urllib.parse import urlparse, parse_qs
23|
24|
25|def main() -> int:
26|    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
27|    parser.add_argument("--tasks-dir", required=True)
28|    parser.add_argument("--runners-file")
29|    parser.add_argument("--deploy-file")
30|    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=0)
31|    parser.add_argument("--port-file", required=True)
32|    args = parser.parse_args()
33|
34|    tasks_dir = pathlib.Path(args.tasks_dir)
35|    fail_ids = set(filter(None, os.environ.get("MOCK_FAIL_IDS", "").split(",")))
36|    badjson_id = os.environ.get("MOCK_BADJSON_ID", "")
37|    mock_empty = os.environ.get("MOCK_EMPTY", "") == "1"
38|
39|    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
40|        def log_message(self, *a):  # keep test output clean
41|            pass
42|
43|        def _send(self, code, body, content_type="application/json"):
44|            data = body.encode()
45|            self.send_response(code)
46|            self.send_header("Content-Type", content_type)
47|            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
48|            self.end_headers()
49|            self.wfile.write(data)
50|
51|        def do_GET(self):
52|            parsed = urlparse(self.path)
53|            path = parsed.path.rstrip("/")
54|            if path == "/tasks":
55|                if mock_empty:
56|                    self._send(200, "[]")
57|                    return
58|                ids = sorted(p.stem for p in tasks_dir.glob("*.json"))
59|                self._send(200, json.dumps([{"id": i} for i in ids]))
60|                return
61|            if path.startswith("/tasks/"):
62|                task_id = path[len("/tasks/"):]
63|                if task_id in fail_ids:
64|                    self._send(500, json.dumps({"error": "mock failure"}))
65|                    return
66|                if task_id == badjson_id:
67|                    self._send(200, "<html>not json</html>", "text/html")
68|                    return
69|                f = tasks_dir / f"{task_id}.json"
70|                if f.is_file():
71|                    self._send(200, f.read_text())
72|                else:
73|                    self._send(404, json.dumps({"error": "no such task"}))
74|                return
75|            if path == "/runners" and args.runners_file:
76|                self._send(200, pathlib.Path(args.runners_file).read_text())
77|                return
78|            if path == "/deploy/status" and args.deploy_file:
79|                self._send(200, pathlib.Path(args.deploy_file).read_text())
80|                return
81|            self._send(404, json.dumps({"error": "not found", "path": path}))
82|
83|    server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", args.port), Handler)
84|    pathlib.Path(args.port_file).write_text(str(server.server_address[1]))
85|    server.serve_forever()
86|    return 0
87|
88|
89|if __name__ == "__main__":
90|    raise SystemExit(main())

24|  reasons: (

29|  )

1|# per-task.jq — turn one raw GET /tasks/<id> payload into one aggregated row.
2|# Consumed by bin/fleet-recount.sh. The output shape is pinned by
3|# bin/tests/run-tests.sh against the recorded before-fixtures — change it
4|# only together with the tests and the before/after tables.
5|#
6|# Defensive notes: every .action access goes through (// "") and runner/reason
7|# extraction uses match() (which yields no output on no-match) instead of
8|# capture() (which hard-errors), so one odd history row can never abort the
9|# whole recount.
10|def ts: if type == "string" then sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601 else null end;
11|def runnerOf($action): [$action | match("Runner (?<r>[^ ]+) interrupted execution") | .captures[0].string] | first // "unknown";
12|def reasonOf($action): if ($action | test("Reason:")) then [$action | match("Reason: (?<x>.*)$") | .captures[0].string] | first else null end;
13|
14|. as $t |
15|# history may be missing or not an array on a malformed payload — treat as
16|# empty rather than aborting the whole recount.
17|def hist: ($t.history // []) | if type == "array" then . else [] end;
18|([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("interrupted execution"))]) as $ints |
19|{
20|  task: $t.id,
21|  status: $t.status,
22|  runner_interrupts: ($ints | length),
23|  with_reason: ([$ints[] | select((.action // "") | test("Reason:"))] | length),
24|  bare: ([$ints[] | select((.action // "") | test("Reason:") | not)] | length),
25|  per_runner: ($ints | map(runnerOf(.action)) | group_by(.) | map({runner: .[0], n: length})),
26|  reasons: ([$ints[] | reasonOf(.action) | select(. != null)] | unique),
27|  auto_resumed: ([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("Auto-resumed after server restart"))] | length),

30|  escalated: ([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("Runner deaths escalated"))] | length),
31|  failed_stage: ([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("Stage failed in|Failed back to stage"))] | length),
32|  git_failure_streak: (($t.gitFailureStreak // {}).count // 0),
33|  last_error_git_kind: ((($t.lastError // {}).gitDiagnostics // {}).kind // null),

{"find":"  # 2. per-task fetch + aggregate row. One bad task never aborts the loop.
  local jsonl="$task_dir/recount-$label.jsonl" errors="$task_dir/recount-$label-errors.jsonl"
  local table="$task_dir/recount-$label-table.json" worklist="$task_dir/recount-$label-e5worklist.json"
  : > "$jsonl"
  : > "$errors"
  local ok=0 failed=0 t raw row_tmp
  row_tmp="$(mktemp)"
  for t in $ids; do
    raw="$raw_dir/$t.json"
    if api_get_json "$api_base/tasks/$t?projectId=$project_id" "$raw" \
       && jq -e 'type == "object" and ((.history // []) | type == "array")' "$raw" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
       && jq -c -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/per-task.jq" "$raw" > "$row_tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
      cat "$row_tmp" >> "$jsonl"
      ok=$((ok + 1))
    else
      failed=$((failed + 1))
      rm -f "$raw"
      printf '{"task":"%s","error":"fetch or parse failed"}\n' "$t" >> "$errors"

{"content":"# S5 ops scripts — fleet recount, runner snapshots, E5 sweep

Read-only evidence tooling for task `683f0bfd` (0.2.x rollout + interrupt
recount). Every script in this folder only READS: the backend API, local git
state, and runner-host worktrees/journals. Nothing here restarts, updates,
reaps, or otherwise mutates any runner or the backend.

## Scripts

| Script | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `fleet-recount.sh <label> [task-dir]` | GUIDE-07 §5 recount + WIDE_NET §2 table over one project. Writes `recount-<label>.jsonl`, `-table.json`, `-e5worklist.json`, `-errors.jsonl`, `-meta.json`, plus `raw/<label>/<taskId>.json` evidence. |
| `runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged]` | Records GET /runners + GET /deploy/status and a per-runner convergence verdict (version ≥ 0.2.x AND build sha contains the fix commit, checked with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`). |
| `e5-sweep.sh <local\|server2> <prefix>...` | GUIDE-05 §4 forensics sweep: per `kb-<taskId>`, reports worktree state, origin refs, stage-output-commit presence, journal lines, and one VERDICT line. |
| `server2-ssh.sh <remote command>` | SSH to the server2-alpha host via `~/.passwrd` without ever printing it. Read-only use only. |
| `lib.sh` | Shared helpers (sourced, never run): logging, validated JSON GET, atomic writes, input guards. |
| `jq/*.jq` | The aggregation rules. `per-task.jq` + `aggregate.jq` output is pinned byte-identical against the recorded before-table by the test suite. |

## Exit codes

- `fleet-recount.sh`: 0 all tasks ok · 1 task list unusable, nothing written · 2 some tasks failed (errors file lists them, table still written)
- `runners-snapshot.sh`: 0 snapshot written · 1 setup/API failure · 3 snapshot written but `--require-converged` not met
- `e5-sweep.sh`: 0 all probed · 1 usage/setup error · 2 some probes failed (per-task VERDICT still printed)
- `server2-ssh.sh`: remote exit code on success · 64 no command · 66 password file missing/empty · 69 no sshpass/pexpect · 124 ssh timeout

## Environment knobs

`KAINBAIN_API_BASE` (default `http://192.168.1.206:3100`),
`KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID`, `KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS`,
`KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT`, `E5_WORK_ROOT`, `E5_UNIT`, `E5_ORIGIN_REPO`,
`E5_JOURNAL_SINCE`. Each script header documents the ones it reads.

## Tests

```sh
bin/tests/run-tests.sh   # offline: recorded fixtures + local mock API, exit 0 = all pass
```

Nothing in the suite touches prod. Re-run it after any change to `*.sh`,
`jq/*.jq`, or `tests/mock-api.py` — T1 fails if the aggregation output
drifts from the recorded before-table.

## Safety rules for operators

1. Observe only — never force-restart a runner mid-assignment from here
   (that would create the very interrupts being measured).
2. A run is trustworthy only when its `*-meta.json` exists and the script's
   exit code was 0 (or an understood 2/3). A missing meta file means the run
   died before publishing; rerun it.
3. Snapshot stamps have second precision; recount labels must be single safe
   path segments (`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*`).

Cleanup complete. The S5 ops toolkit ([bin/](docs/tasks/683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c/bin/README.md)) is hardened and fully green: the offline suite went from 71 to 95 passing checks with zero failures, and both recorded baselines (before-table via the suite, mid-1431 table plus E5 worklist via an independent rerun) reproduce byte-exactly, so aggregation behavior did not regress.

The suite itself gained an EXIT trap that kills mock servers, clear failures for missing fixtures/tags/unstarted mocks, and no longer parses `ls`. I also reverted the one out-of-scope line in [useOnboarding.test.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c/frontend/src/hooks/useOnboarding.test.js) (now identical to `main`) and added a `bin/README.md` ops handoff covering purpose, exit codes, env knobs, and the observe-only safety rules.

Read text file `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`.
1|# Runner update runbook
2|
3|Operator procedures for the runner self-update channel (Option A,
4|`docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md`): cutting releases,
5|rolling back, migrating hosts to the wrapper, and triaging a runner
6|that says out of date. The backend directs version selection but never
7|serves runner bytes (R05) — every procedure below preserves that.
8|
9|## Cutting a runner release (normal path)
10|
11|The tag is the version source of truth; the pipeline cuts it.
12|
13|1. Bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json` (plain semver for
14|   fleet releases, e.g. `0.2.0`; suffixed tags like `0.3.0-rc.1` for
15|   canaries — v1 runners skip pre-releases automatically).
16|2. If the release needs a newer backend API, update the
17|   `requires.backendApi` range in the same file (e.g.
18|   `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`). The release builder refuses manifests without a
19|   compat claim, and runners filter on this range.
20|3. Merge to the main line through the normal review flow.
21|4. Publish the runner (`publish.sh` with the runner component). The
22|   publish cuts and pushes the annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which
23|   triggers `runner-release.yml`: full update-channel test gate, four
24|   platform archives, signed `manifest.json` + `.minisig`, GitHub
25|   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
26|   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).
27|5. Raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the new version on
28|   the backend. That is the one managed place: trailers light the
29|   "update available" badge and the backend auto-nudges command-capable
30|   ones (`requestUpdate`, at most daily per runner). Runners converge
31|   on idle with no SSH. Leave `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` alone
32|   unless this is a breaking release (the 409 floor stops dispatch).
33|
34|## Cutting a runner release (emergency path)
35|
36|When the pipeline cannot cut the tag (CI down, urgent patch), tag by
37|hand from the release commit — the same builder runs:
38|
39|```
40|git tag -a runner-vX.Y.Z -m "Runner runner-vX.Y.Z" <full-sha>
41|git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z
42|```
43|
44|Then follow step 5 above. Never move an existing tag: cut a patch
45|version forward instead.
46|
47|## Rollback drill (bad release, no host access needed)
48|
49|1. Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release so `releases/latest`
50|   resolves to the prior tag.
51|2. Lower `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (and
52|   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` if it was raised past the bad
53|   version) to stop badge nagging and 409 loops.
54|3. Cut a patch release forward (normal path above). The updater never
55|   downgrades: runners still on older versions pick the prior release
56|   up on their next idle check, while runners already on the bad
57|   release stay there until the patch supersedes it.
58|4. Two automatic outs: a release that crashes on boot rolls itself
59|   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
60|   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
61|   is cut.
62|
63|Drill timing to record: un-publish → badges clear, patch cut →
64|fleet converged.
65|
66|## Migrating a host to the wrapper
67|
68|Direct `node main.js` units re-exec the same old directory on every
69|restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
70|versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at
71|the stable wrapper shim — onto the SAME version (no update is staged,
72|so the fleet version does not change).
73|
74|Per host, idle runners first; drain busy runners, then migrate:
75|
76|```
77|# 1. Pre-check (read-only, safe any time):
78|KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT=$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install \
79|  /path/to/runner/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service
80|
81|# 2. Rehearse:
82|scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id> --dry-run
83|
84|# 3. Migrate (snapshots unit + env, reloads, restarts, re-verifies):
85|scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id>
86|```
87|
88|The script refuses to overwrite an existing `current` link and prints
89|revert commands (copy the `.bak-<timestamp>` files back, reload,
90|restart). New installs need no migration: both installers
91|(`scripts/install-local-runner.sh`, `startRunner.sh`) already write
92|wrapper-based units. Verify after: `doctor` reports `status: ok` with
93|`entrypoint: wrapper`, and the next heartbeat shows the same version
94|as before.
95|
96|## Restart vs Update (Settings › Runners)
97|
98|Two separate actions, never combined:
99|
100|- **Restart** reboots the runner on its **current version** — no update
101|  check runs. It is destructive: any work running on that runner is
102|  stopped at once (the claim lease expires so the work re-queues, like a
103|  crash). The confirm window names the runner and warns about running
104|  work; use it when a runner looks stuck, not to change versions.
105|  Mechanism: the daemon writes a `restart-requested` sentinel beside the
106|  install root and exits 0; the wrapper consumes it and boots the SAME
107|  tree again. Restart therefore needs the wrapper entrypoint — a runner
108|  started as bare `node main.js` exits without rebooting (migrate to the
109|  wrapper, above).
110|- **Update** reinstalls the runner onto its **target version** — the
111|  exact pin when the runner is pinned, otherwise the newest compatible
112|  release — and applies only when the runner is idle (never interrupts
113|  work). A busy runner queues the update for the next idle point.
114|
115|## Per-runner version setting
116|
117|Each runner is set to **Latest** (default) or one exact release, via
118|the version dropdown on its Settings › Runners detail panel:
119|
120|- **Latest** tracks the newest release. It auto-updates at the next
121|  idle point (including right after a restart, once idle), and the
122|  backend nudges trailing runners at most daily. A red banner appears
123|  whenever a newer version exists than the one running — update (or
124|  wait for idle) to converge it.
125|- **Pinned** stays on exactly that release. Pinned runners never
126|  auto-update (no nudges, no idle installs, no restart-time installs);
127|  only the manual **Update** button installs the pin, and only when the
128|  pin is newer than the running version — the channel never downgrades,
129|  so a pin older than running shows a softer warning and the Update
130|  button stays disabled with the reason. Pick Latest or a newer pin to
131|  move forward.
132|
133|The dropdown lists Latest plus every fleet-known release (newest
134|first): each runner's running version plus the fleet recommended and
135|minimum knobs — offline-safe, no release catalogue fetch.
136|
137|## Triage: a runner says out of date
138|
139|Start on the runner host (or ask the host owner to run it) — the
140|doctor is read-only and never writes:
141|
142|```
143|$KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service
144|```
145|
146|Match the Settings › Runners badge to a cause:
147|
148|- **"update available" that never clears.** The runner trails
149|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (Latest runners) or its pin.
150|  If the doctor says `entrypoint: direct`, migrate to the wrapper
151|  (above) — staged updates can never boot there. If the env shows
152|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` (or `(unset)` with a host-level
153|  opt-out), the runner acked the nudge with "skipped: auto-update is
154|  disabled" — flip that switch. If the runner is pinned, only the
155|  manual Update button installs (pins never auto-update); a pin older
156|  than running refuses with "never downgrades" — pick Latest or a
157|  newer pin. If the recommended knob sits above every published
158|  release, lower it to the newest release. Otherwise the runner is
159|  likely just busy: it converges at the next idle check, or press
160|  Update now (idle-only, never interrupts work). Restart does NOT
161|  clear this — Restart reboots the same version.
162|- **"restart queued" that never clears / restart loop.** The runner
163|  collects `requestRestart` on every heartbeat but never reboots:
164|  check the journal for the `Runner restarting` line. If the line is
165|  there but no reboot follows, the runner is not supervised by the
166|  wrapper (bare `node main.js` exits instead of rebooting — migrate to
167|  the wrapper, above) or the install root is unwritable (look for
168|  `sentinel not written`). A `restart-requested` file left behind by a
169|  crash causes at most one extra boot on the next clean exit — the
170|  wrapper consumes it, never loops. Old runners that predate the
171|  command show a disabled Restart with "too old" guidance instead —
172|  update them manually.
173|- **"below minimum" / 409 loop.** The runner is under
174|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` and dispatch refuses it. It
175|  self-updates immediately when idle (interval bypassed). If it
176|  spins, check the journal for `Runner update` lines and treat the
177|  reason like an "update failed" below.
178|- **"update failed".** The next heartbeat carries `updateStatus`
179|  (`state: failed`, `reason`, `at`) — the badge tooltip shows it.
180|  Map the reason prefix: signature/key failure (release not signed
181|  by the pinned key — never hand-edit
182|  `PINNED_RELEASE_PUBLIC_KEY` in `runner/updates/verify.js` for a
183|  cut release); sha mismatch (re-download on next check); no asset
184|  for this platform (release is missing this host's tarball);
185|  incompatible with this backend (no newer release admits this
186|  backend's API — expected while the backend lags the release
187|  line); update lock held (a previous updater is still running or
188|  crashed mid-apply — stale locks self-heal); opted out (see
189|  above). Any failure keeps the old version running; fix the cause
190|  and the next idle check retries.
191|- **"rolled back" in the doctor.** Three crashed boots flipped
192|  `current` back to `previous`. Do not retry blindly: read the
193|  journal for the crash, fix forward with a patch release, and run
194|  the rollback drill above if the release is bad fleet-wide.
195|
196|Backend-side checks: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` and
197|`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` values, the fleet matrix row
198|for the runner (`runnerVersion`, `updateAvailable`, `belowMinimum`,
199|`updateStatus`), and whether a `requestUpdate` command is pending or
200|was acked within the last 24h (the auto-nudge cooldown).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# fleet-recount.sh <label> [task-dir] — GUIDE-07 §5 fleet recount +
# WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table, over one project, read-only against the
# backend API (approved: this task's SURVEY.md q2). Scope is pinned to project
# 0fd41821-... so results compare directly with the 2026-11-21 baseline.
#
# Outputs (under task-dir, default: current directory):
#   raw/<label>/<taskId>.json        raw GET /tasks/<id> payloads (evidence)
#   recount-<label>.jsonl            one aggregated row per task  (jq/per-task.jq)
#   recount-<label>-table.json       WIDE_NET §2 aggregate         (jq/aggregate.jq)
#   recount-<label>-e5worklist.json  post-finished interrupts      (jq/e5-worklist.jq, GUIDE-05 §4 scope)
#   recount-<label>-errors.jsonl     tasks that failed to fetch/parse (always created; empty when nothing failed)
#   recount-<label>-meta.json        run metadata (api, project, window, counts)
#   stdout                           the §2 table + E5 worklist, for the run log
#
# Crash safety: per-task rows accumulate in temp staging files and are moved
# into place only after the fetch loop finishes, so killing the script
# mid-run can never leave a truncated recount-<label>.jsonl beside a
# meta/table from an older run of the same label.
#
# Failure behaviour (deliberate, so a partial run is loud, never silent):
#   - the task list itself unreachable/invalid/empty -> exit 1, no outputs written
#   - one task fails to download or parse -> recorded in -errors.jsonl, the
#     loop continues, the table is still written, and the script exits 2 at
#     the end so the gap cannot be missed
#   - API base / project overridable via KAINBAIN_API_BASE / KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID
#     (the test suite drives this script against a local mock API)
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

main() {
  require_commands curl jq date mktemp
  local label="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$label" ] || die "usage: fleet-recount.sh <before|after|...> [task-dir]"
  [ $# -le 2 ] || die "usage: fleet-recount.sh <before|after|...> [task-dir] — unexpected extra argument '$3'"
  validate_label "$label"
  local task_dir="${2:-$(pwd)}"
  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
  local project_id="${KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID:-0fd41821-d8a5-4e49-bc2e-28ce8c739a0a}"
  local raw_dir="$task_dir/raw/$label"
  mkdir -p "$raw_dir"
  local started; started="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  log "fleet-recount label=$label api=$api_base project=$project_id task_dir=$task_dir started=$started"

  # 1. task list — must be a non-empty array of well-formed ids, otherwise the
  #    API is down, the project id is wrong, or we got an error page.
  local list_tmp; list_tmp="$(mktemp)"
  if ! api_get_json "$api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id" "$list_tmp.list"; then
    rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
    die "cannot list tasks at $api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id — API down or wrong project; nothing written"
  fi
  local ids; ids="$(jq -r 'if type == "array" then (.[].id // empty) else empty end' "$list_tmp.list")"
  rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
  local n; n="$(printf '%s
' "$ids" | grep -c . || true)"
  [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || die "GET /tasks returned zero tasks for project $project_id — refusing to write an empty baseline"
  if printf '%s
' "$ids" | grep -qvE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'; then
    die "task list contains a malformed id — refusing to continue (got: $(printf '%s
' "$ids" | grep -vE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' | head -3 | tr '
' ' '))"
  fi
  log "task list ok: $n tasks"

  # 2. per-task fetch + aggregate row. One bad task never aborts the loop.
  # Rows accumulate in staging files first (see header: crash safety).
  local jsonl="$task_dir/recount-$label.jsonl" errors="$task_dir/recount-$label-errors.jsonl"
  local table="$task_dir/recount-$label-table.json" worklist="$task_dir/recount-$label-e5worklist.json"
  local jsonl_stage errors_stage row_tmp
  jsonl_stage="$(mktemp)"; errors_stage="$(mktemp)"; row_tmp="$(mktemp)"

# lib.sh — shared helpers for the S5 ops scripts in this folder (bin/).
# Sourced, never executed directly. Shared because every script here needs
# the same three things: loud logging, loud death, and a validated HTTP GET.
#
# Rule for this task folder: an ops evidence script must never silently
# degrade. Every helper below either succeeds completely or reports a clear
# error and returns non-zero, so a baseline built from these scripts is
# trustworthy.

# log <message...> — timestamped progress line on stderr. stdout stays clean
# because the scripts print evidence tables (jsonl/tsv) on stdout.
log() {
  printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" >&2
}

# die <message...> — report a clear, fatal setup/usage error and exit 1.
# Used where there is nothing to salvage (missing tool, unreachable API,
# bad arguments). Runtime per-item failures are handled by the callers
# (recorded, counted, non-zero exit at the end) — see fleet-recount.sh.
die() {
  log "FATAL: $*"
  exit 1
}

# require_commands <cmd...> — fail before touching anything if a tool is
# missing, so the failure is about the environment, not about half-written
# evidence files.
require_commands() {
  local missing=() cmd
  for cmd in "$@"; do
    command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$cmd")
  done
  if [ "${#missing[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    die "missing required commands: ${missing[*]} — install them or run on the runner host"
  fi
}

# write_atomic <dest> <src-file> — copy src-file next to dest and rename over
# it, so a crashed run never leaves a half-written evidence file that looks
# complete. Same directory => the final mv is an atomic rename.
# Returns non-zero (and leaves dest untouched) when either step fails.
write_atomic() {
  # NOTE: tmp gets its own statement on purpose. `local dest="$1" ...
  # tmp="$dest.tmp.$$"` in ONE declaration does NOT see the just-assigned
  # dest — bash expands it from the caller's scope, so it only worked while
  # every caller happened to have its own $dest (and died with
  # `dest: unbound variable` otherwise). Separate statements, no surprise.
  local dest="$1" src="$2" tmp
  tmp="$dest.tmp.$$"
  if ! cp "$src" "$tmp"; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: cannot write $dest (copy step failed)"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! mv "$tmp" "$dest"; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: cannot write $dest (rename step failed)"
    return 1
  fi
}

# api_get_json <url> <dest> — GET url into dest as validated JSON.
#   - retries transient network failures (curl --retry-connrefused)
#   - fails on any HTTP error status (curl -f, so a 500/404 body is NOT kept)
#   - refuses to store a 200 body that is not valid JSON (an HTML error page
#     must never end up in the evidence store)
#   - writes dest atomically
# Returns non-zero with a clear stderr line on any failure.
api_get_json() {
  local url="$1" dest="$2" tmp
  tmp="$(mktemp)"
  if ! curl -sfS -m 60 --retry 3 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 2 -o "$tmp" "$url"; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: GET $url failed (HTTP error or host unreachable after retries)"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! jq -e 'type == "object" or type == "array"' "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: GET $url returned a body that is not valid JSON — refusing to store it in $dest"
    return 1
  fi
  # Propagate the write result explicitly: without this, the status of the
  # `rm` below would mask a failed store and the caller would trust a file
  # that was never written.
  local write_rc=0
  write_atomic "$dest" "$tmp" || write_rc=$?
  rm -f "$tmp"
  return "$write_rc"
}

# validate_label <label> — recount/snapshot labels become file- and directory
# names (recount-<label>.jsonl, raw/<label>/...), so they must be a single
# safe path segment. Without this a label like "../../x" would write evidence
# outside the task folder.
validate_label() {
  local label="$1"
  if ! [[ "$label" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ ]]; then
    die "bad label '$label' — use letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore only, starting with a letter or digit (e.g. before, mid-1431)"
  fi
}

# validate_task_prefix <prefix...> — task ids/prefixes get interpolated into
# shell commands (locally and over ssh) by e5-sweep.sh, so they must be hex
# and dashes only. Accepts a short prefix (8 hex chars) or a full UUID.
# This is the injection guard for the sweep: anything else is rejected before
# any command runs.
validate_task_prefix() {
  local p
  for p in "$@"; do
    if ! [[ "$p" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}(-[0-9a-fA-F]{4,12})*$ ]]; then
      die "bad task id prefix '$p' — expected 8 hex chars plus optional -hex groups (e.g. 7f6220c3 or the full UUID)"
    fi
  done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — record the fleet matrix
# (GET /runners + GET /deploy/status) and a per-runner convergence verdict.
# READ-ONLY against the backend; safe to run any time, any number of times.
#
# Outputs in <outdir>:
#   runners-<stamp>.json        raw GET /runners payload (evidence)
#   runners-<stamp>.tsv         flat fleet table incl. build sha/builtAt
#   deploy-status-<stamp>.json  raw GET /deploy/status payload
#   verdict-<stamp>.txt         one line per named runner: CONVERGED or the reasons why not
#
# Convergence rule (S5 success criterion 1): runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND the
# running build's reported git sha contains the fix commit — verified locally
# with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fixCommit> <buildSha>`, because a version
# string alone cannot prove which code is running. If the runner reports no
# build sha, the verdict says so instead of guessing.
#
# Knobs (env):
#   KAINBAIN_API_BASE            default http://192.168.1.206:3100
#   KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS    default "local-alpha,server2-alpha"
#   KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT       default 046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4 (the 046a6391 deterministic-git-failure change)
#
# Exit codes: 0 snapshot written (converged or not — read verdict-<stamp>.txt);
#   1 setup or API failure (nothing trustworthy written);
#   3 snapshot written, --require-converged given, but not all named runners converged.
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

# fix_in_build <buildSha|""|null> — prints true/false/null. null = cannot tell
# (no sha reported, or sha unknown to the local repo). Uses the local Kainbain
# checkout as the commit database — read-only git queries only.
fix_in_build() {
  local sha="$1" repo_root="$2" fix_commit="$3"
  if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ "$sha" = "null" ]; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if ! git -C "$repo_root" cat-file -e "$sha^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if git -C "$repo_root" merge-base --is-ancestor "$fix_commit" "$sha" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo true
  else
    echo false
  fi
}

# verdict_for <runners.json> <runnerId> — prints the verdict JSON object for one
# runner (jq/runner-verdict.jq + the git ancestry check).
verdict_for() {
  local runners_json="$1" runner_id="$2" repo_root="$3" fix_commit="$4"
  local runner sha fix
  runner="$(jq -c --arg id "$runner_id" '.[] | select(.runnerId == $id) // empty' "$runners_json")"
  if [ -z "$runner" ]; then
    printf '{"runnerId":"%s","converged":false,"reasons":["runner not present in GET /runners (offline/revoked?)"]}\n' "$runner_id"
    return 0
  fi
  sha="$(printf '%s' "$runner" | jq -r '.facts.versions.build.sha // ""')"
  fix="$(fix_in_build "$sha" "$repo_root" "$fix_commit")"
  jq -n -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/runner-verdict.jq" --argjson runner "$runner" --argjson fixInBuild "$fix"
}

main() {
  require_commands curl jq git date mktemp
  local outdir="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$outdir" ] || die "usage: runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged]"
  local require_converged=0
  if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
    [ "$2" = "--require-converged" ] || die "usage: runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — unexpected argument '$2'"
    require_converged=1
  fi
  [ $# -le 2 ] || die "usage: runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — unexpected extra argument '$3'"

  local named="${KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS:-local-alpha,server2-alpha}"

  local task_dir repo_root stamp
  task_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"

  # Second precision: two snapshots in the same minute must not overwrite each other.
  stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
  mkdir -p "$outdir"

  local runners_json="$outdir/runners-$stamp.json" deploy_json="$outdir/deploy-status-$stamp.json"

  # envelope, an HTML page that slipped through) would make every downstream
  # verdict meaningless, so stop here with a clear message.
  if ! jq -e 'type == "array"' "$runners_json" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rm -f "$runners_json"
    die "GET $api_base/runners returned valid JSON that is not an array — refusing to build a verdict from it"

    else
      all_converged=0
      printf 'NOT-CONVERGED %s — %s\n' "$r" "$(printf '%s' "$v" | jq -r '.reasons | join("; ")')" >> "$verdict_body"
    fi
  done
  jq -s '.' "$verdict_json.tmp.$$" > "$verdict_json" && rm -f "$verdict_json.tmp.$$"

  {
    echo "# runner convergence verdict — $(date -u +%FT%TZ) — fix commit $fix_commit"
    echo "# converged = runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND running build sha contains the fix commit"
    cat "$verdict_body"

    echo "wrote $outdir/runners-$stamp.{json,tsv} $outdir/deploy-status-$stamp.json $outdir/verdict-$stamp.{json,txt}"
  else
    echo "wrote $outdir/runners-$stamp.{json,tsv} $outdir/verdict-$stamp.{json,txt} (no deploy-status: GET /deploy/status failed)"
  fi
  cat "$outdir/runners-$stamp.tsv"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# e5-sweep.sh <local|server2> <taskId-prefix>... — GUIDE-05 §4 E5 forensics
# sweep. READ-ONLY: it never reaps, deletes, restarts, updates, or modifies
# anything on either host (survey q9: observe only). For each kb-<taskId>
# it records, per host:
#   - worktrees under the work root: existence + git log + whether a
#     stage-output commit is present in HEAD history
#   - origin branch refs (refs/remotes/origin/kb/<id>* and kb-<id>*): the
#     durable evidence that survives worktree reaping, with git log
#
# Stage-output detection is scoped to the task's OWN branch: a commit counts
# only if its subject matches ^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output. Merged/mirrored
# history regularly contains OTHER tasks' stage-output commits (observed in
# the 2026-11-23 before-sweep: kb/1cae113f commits inside kb/7f6220c3 refs),
# and an unscoped grep would flip the verdict to a false Cause 2/4.
#   - journal lines for the task id (Runner failed / commit / hook / 413 /
#     502 / fetch failed / interrupt)
# and prints one VERDICT line per task:
#   stage-output commit PRESENT  -> Cause 2/4 territory (GUIDE-05 §4)
#   evidence found, commit ABSENT -> Cause 5 suspect (commit/push loop with no landed output)
#   no worktree and no origin ref -> evidence gap (reaped/branch deleted)
#
# Safety: task-id arguments are validated (hex/dashes only — injection guard,
# see lib.sh) and the remote probe is sent base64-encoded, so no argument can
# break out of the remote shell. The probe itself runs only ls/git
# log/for-each-ref/journalctl — all read-only.
#
# Usage:
#   bin/e5-sweep.sh local   7f6220c3 db49d6c6 ...
#   bin/e5-sweep.sh server2 158394ab ...
# Env overrides (used by the test suite, harmless in prod):
#   E5_WORK_ROOT  E5_UNIT  E5_ORIGIN_REPO  E5_JOURNAL_SINCE
# Exit codes: 0 all probed; 1 usage/setup error; 2 some probes failed (output
# still written — the summary says which).
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

# The probe body. Fixed text — the only variables are its five positional
# arguments, all validated or script-controlled before this runs anywhere.
PROBE_SCRIPT='
set -uo pipefail
WORK_ROOT="$1"; UNIT="$2"; ORIGIN_REPO="$3"; PREFIX="$4"; SINCE="$5"
stage_present=0; any_evidence=0

echo "== task kb-$PREFIX"
echo "-- worktrees under $WORK_ROOT:"
found=0
for d in "$WORK_ROOT"/kb-"$PREFIX"*; do
  [ -d "$d" ] || continue
  found=1; any_evidence=1
  echo "   worktree: $d (branch: $(git -C "$d" branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo "?"))"
  git -C "$d" log --format="     %h %ci %s" -5 2>&1 | head -6 || true
  # NB: grep WITHOUT -q on purpose — under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` exits on
  # the first match, git log gets SIGPIPE (rc 141), and the pipeline reports
  # failure even when a match existed. Plain grep reads all input: rc 0 = match.
  if git -C "$d" log --format=%s -20 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output" >/dev/null; then
    stage_present=1
    echo "     stage-output-commit: PRESENT in worktree HEAD history (subject ^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output)"
  else
    echo "     stage-output-commit: absent in worktree HEAD history"
  fi
  for ref in $(git -C "$d" for-each-ref --format="%(refname)" "refs/remotes/origin/kb/$PREFIX"* "refs/remotes/origin/kb-$PREFIX"* 2>/dev/null); do
    echo "   origin ref: $ref"
    git -C "$d" log --format="     %h %ci %s" -5 "$ref" 2>&1 | head -6 || true
    if git -C "$d" log --format=%s -20 "$ref" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output" >/dev/null; then
      stage_present=1
      echo "     stage-output-commit: PRESENT on $ref (subject ^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output)"
    else
      echo "     stage-output-commit: absent on $ref"
    fi
  done
done
[ "$found" = 1 ] || echo "   (no worktree on this host)"

echo "-- origin branch refs in $ORIGIN_REPO (durable, survives worktree reaping):"
if git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  refs=$(git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" for-each-ref --format="%(refname)" "refs/remotes/origin/kb/$PREFIX"* "refs/remotes/origin/kb-$PREFIX"* "refs/heads/kb/$PREFIX"* "refs/heads/kb-$PREFIX"* 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "$refs" ]; then
    any_evidence=1
    while IFS= read -r ref; do
      echo "   $ref"
      git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" log --format="     %h %ci %s" -8 "$ref" 2>&1 | head -9 || true
      if git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" log --format=%s -20 "$ref" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output" >/dev/null; then
        stage_present=1
        echo "     stage-output-commit: PRESENT on $ref (subject ^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output)"
      else
        echo "     stage-output-commit: absent on $ref"
      fi
    done <<EOF
$refs
EOF
  else
    echo "   (no origin branch kb/$PREFIX* or kb-$PREFIX*)"
  fi
else
  echo "   (origin repo $ORIGIN_REPO not available on this host — evidence gap note)"
fi

echo "-- journal ($UNIT, since $SINCE) lines matching $PREFIX:"
if command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  journalctl --user -u "$UNIT" --since "$SINCE" --no-pager 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -i -- "$PREFIX" | grep -iE "Runner failed|commit|hook|413|502|fetch failed|interrupt" | tail -15 | sed "s/^/   /" \
    || echo "   (no matching journal lines)"
else
  echo "   (journalctl not available on this host)"
fi

if [ "$stage_present" = 1 ]; then
  echo "VERDICT kb-$PREFIX: stage-output commit PRESENT -> Cause 2/4 territory (GUIDE-05 §4)"
elif [ "$any_evidence" = 1 ]; then
  echo "VERDICT kb-$PREFIX: evidence found but no stage-output commit -> Cause 5 suspect (commit/push loop, no landed output)"
else
  echo "VERDICT kb-$PREFIX: no worktree and no origin branch -> evidence gap (worktree reaped and branch deleted)"
fi
echo
'

# run_probe <host> <work_root> <unit> <origin_repo> <prefix> <since>
# Local: pipe the probe into bash directly. server2: base64-encode the probe
# and decode it on the remote side, so argument quoting can never inject.
run_probe() {
  local host="$1"; shift
  local args; args="$(printf '%q ' "$@")"
  if [ "$host" = "server2" ]; then
    local b64
    b64="$(printf '%s' "$PROBE_SCRIPT" | base64 -w0)"
    "$SCRIPT_DIR/server2-ssh.sh" "echo $b64 | base64 -d | bash -s -- $args"
  else
    printf '%s' "$PROBE_SCRIPT" | bash -s -- "$@"
  fi
}

main() {
  require_commands bash base64 date git
  local host="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$host" ] || die "usage: e5-sweep.sh <local|server2> <taskId-prefix>..."
  [ "$host" = "local" ] || [ "$host" = "server2" ] || die "host must be 'local' or 'server2', got '$host'"
  shift
  [ $# -ge 1 ] || die "usage: e5-sweep.sh <local|server2> <taskId-prefix>... (at least one task id)"
  validate_task_prefix "$@"

  local task_dir repo_root work_root unit origin_repo since
  task_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
  repo_root="$(git -C "$task_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
  since="${E5_JOURNAL_SINCE:-2026-11-19}"
  if [ "$host" = "server2" ]; then
    work_root="${E5_WORK_ROOT:-/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work}"
    unit="${E5_UNIT:-kainbain-runner-server2-alpha}"
    origin_repo="${E5_ORIGIN_REPO:-/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/mirrors/Kainbain}"
  else
    work_root="${E5_WORK_ROOT:-$HOME/.kainbain/runner-work}"
    unit="${E5_UNIT:-kainbain-runner-local-alpha}"
    origin_repo="${E5_ORIGIN_REPO:-$repo_root}"
  fi

  echo "## E5 sweep host=$host work_root=$work_root unit=$unit origin_repo=$origin_repo since=$since at $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  local failed=0 t
  for t in "$@"; do
    if ! run_probe "$host" "$work_root" "$unit" "$origin_repo" "$t" "$since"; then
      failed=$((failed + 1))
      log "WARN: probe for kb-$t on $host failed — recorded, continuing with the next task"
      echo "VERDICT kb-$t: PROBE FAILED on $host (see stderr) — treat as evidence gap"
      echo
    fi
  done
  echo "## E5 sweep done: $# task(s), $failed probe failure(s) at $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
    log "exiting 2: $failed probe(s) failed"
    exit 2
  fi
}

if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
  main "$@"
fi

#   recount-<label>-table.json       WIDE_NET §2 aggregate         (jq/aggregate.jq)
#   recount-<label>-e5worklist.json  post-finished interrupts      (jq/e5-worklist.jq, GUIDE-05 §4 scope)
#   recount-<label>-errors.jsonl     tasks that failed to fetch/parse (always created; empty when nothing failed)
#   recount-<label>-meta.json        run metadata (api, project, window, counts)
#   stdout                           the §2 table + E5 worklist, for the run log
#
# Crash safety: per-task rows accumulate in temp staging files and are moved
# into place only after the fetch loop finishes, so killing the script
# mid-run can never leave a truncated recount-<label>.jsonl beside a
# meta/table from an older run of the same label.
#
# Failure behaviour (deliberate, so a partial run is loud, never silent):
#   - the task list itself unreachable/invalid/empty -> exit 1, no outputs written
#   - one task fails to download or parse -> recorded in -errors.jsonl, the
#     loop continues, the table is still written, and the script exits 2 at

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

main() {
  require_commands curl jq date mktemp
  local label="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$label" ] || die "usage: fleet-recount.sh <before|after|...> [task-dir]"
  [ $# -le 2 ] || die "usage: fleet-recount.sh <before|after|...> [task-dir] — unexpected extra argument '$3'"
  validate_label "$label"
  local task_dir="${2:-$(pwd)}"
  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
  local project_id="${KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID:-0fd41821-d8a5-4e49-bc2e-28ce8c739a0a}"

  log "fleet-recount label=$label api=$api_base project=$project_id task_dir=$task_dir started=$started"

  # 1. task list — must be a non-empty array of well-formed ids, otherwise the
  #    API is down, the project id is wrong, or we got an error page.
  local list_tmp; list_tmp="$(mktemp)"
  if ! api_get_json "$api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id" "$list_tmp.list"; then
    rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
    die "cannot list tasks at $api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id — API down or wrong project; nothing written"

' "$ids" | grep -c . || true)"

' "$ids" | grep -qvE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'; then
    die "task list contains a malformed id — refusing to continue (got: $(printf '%s
' "$ids" | grep -vE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' | head -3 | tr '
' ' '))"
  fi
  log "task list ok: $n tasks"

  # Rows accumulate in staging files first (see header: crash safety).
  local jsonl="$task_dir/recount-$label.jsonl" errors="$task_dir/recount-$label-errors.jsonl"
  local table="$task_dir/recount-$label-table.json" worklist="$task_dir/recount-$label-e5worklist.json"
  local jsonl_stage errors_stage row_tmp
  jsonl_stage="$(mktemp)"; errors_stage="$(mktemp)"; row_tmp="$(mktemp)"

    raw="$raw_dir/$t.json"

      log "WARN: task $t failed to fetch/parse — recorded in recount-$label-errors.jsonl, continuing"
    fi
  done
  rm -f "$row_tmp"
  write_atomic "$jsonl" "$jsonl_stage" || die "cannot publish $jsonl — previous file (if any) left untouched"

  rm -f "$jsonl_stage" "$errors_stage"
  log "fetched $ok tasks, $failed failed"

  # 3. aggregates (atomic writes), printed to stdout for the run log too.
  jq -s -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/aggregate.jq" "$jsonl" > "$table.tmp.$$" && mv "$table.tmp.$$" "$table"
  jq -s -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/e5-worklist.jq" "$jsonl" > "$worklist.tmp.$$" && mv "$worklist.tmp.$$" "$worklist"
  jq -n --arg label "$label" --arg api "$api_base" --arg project "$project_id" \
      --arg started "$started" --arg finished "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" \
      --argjson ok "$ok" --argjson failed "$failed" \
      '{label: $label, api: $api, project: $project, startedAt: $started, finishedAt: $finished, tasksFetched: $ok, tasksFailed: $failed}' \
    > "$task_dir/recount-$label-meta.json"

  echo "## WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table — label=$label, project $project_id, $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  jq . "$table"
  echo
  echo "## E5 worklist — post-finished interrupts (GUIDE-05 §4 scope), label=$label"
  jq . "$worklist"
  echo
  if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "## ERRORS — $failed task(s) failed, see recount-$label-errors.jsonl" >&2
    cat "$errors" >&2
    log "exiting 2: $failed of $n tasks failed"
    exit 2
  fi
  log "done: label=$label ok=$ok failed=$failed"
}

  main "$@"
fi

      cat "$row_tmp" >> "$jsonl_stage"
      ok=$((ok + 1))
    else
      failed=$((failed + 1))
      rm -f "$raw"
      printf '{"task":"%s","error":"fetch or parse failed"}\n' "$t" >> "$errors_stage"
      log "WARN: task $t failed to fetch/parse — recorded in recount-$label-errors.jsonl, continuing"
    fi
  done
  rm -f "$row_tmp"
  write_atomic "$jsonl" "$jsonl_stage" || die "cannot publish $jsonl — previous file (if any) left untouched"
  write_atomic "$errors" "$errors_stage" || die "cannot publish $errors — $jsonl was published, rerun to regenerate"
  rm -f "$jsonl_stage" "$errors_stage"
  log "fetched $ok tasks, $failed failed"

  # 3. aggregates (atomic writes), printed to stdout for the run log too.
  jq -s -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/aggregate.jq" "$jsonl" > "$table.tmp.$$" && mv "$table.tmp.$$" "$table"
  jq -s -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/e5-worklist.jq" "$jsonl" > "$worklist.tmp.$$" && mv "$worklist.tmp.$$" "$worklist"
  jq -n --arg label "$label" --arg api "$api_base" --arg project "$project_id" \
      --arg started "$started" --arg finished "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" \
      --argjson ok "$ok" --argjson failed "$failed" \
      '{label: $label, api: $api, project: $project, startedAt: $started, finishedAt: $finished, tasksFetched: $ok, tasksFailed: $failed}' \
    > "$task_dir/recount-$label-meta.json"

  echo "## WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table — label=$label, project $project_id, $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  jq . "$table"
  echo
  echo "## E5 worklist — post-finished interrupts (GUIDE-05 §4 scope), label=$label"
  jq . "$worklist"
  echo
  if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "## ERRORS — $failed task(s) failed, see recount-$label-errors.jsonl" >&2
    cat "$errors" >&2
    log "exiting 2: $failed of $n tasks failed"
    exit 2
  fi
  log "done: label=$label ok=$ok failed=$failed"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# lib.sh — shared helpers for the S5 ops scripts in this folder (bin/).
# Sourced, never executed directly. Shared because every script here needs
# the same three things: loud logging, loud death, and a validated HTTP GET.
#
# Rule for this task folder: an ops evidence script must never silently
# degrade. Every helper below either succeeds completely or reports a clear
# error and returns non-zero, so a baseline built from these scripts is
# trustworthy.

# log <message...> — timestamped progress line on stderr. stdout stays clean
# because the scripts print evidence tables (jsonl/tsv) on stdout.
log() {
  printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" >&2
}

# die <message...> — report a clear, fatal setup/usage error and exit 1.
# Used where there is nothing to salvage (missing tool, unreachable API,
# bad arguments). Runtime per-item failures are handled by the callers
# (recorded, counted, non-zero exit at the end) — see fleet-recount.sh.
die() {
  log "FATAL: $*"
  exit 1
}

# require_commands <cmd...> — fail before touching anything if a tool is
# missing, so the failure is about the environment, not about half-written
# evidence files.
require_commands() {
  local missing=() cmd
  for cmd in "$@"; do
    command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$cmd")
  done
  if [ "${#missing[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    die "missing required commands: ${missing[*]} — install them or run on the runner host"
  fi
}

# write_atomic <dest> <src-file> — copy src-file next to dest and rename over
# it, so a crashed run never leaves a half-written evidence file that looks
# complete. Same directory => the final mv is an atomic rename.
# Returns non-zero (and leaves dest untouched) when either step fails.
write_atomic() {
  # NOTE: tmp gets its own statement on purpose. `local dest="$1" ...
  # tmp="$dest.tmp.$$"` in ONE declaration does NOT see the just-assigned
  # dest — bash expands it from the caller's scope, so it only worked while
  # every caller happened to have its own $dest (and died with
  # `dest: unbound variable` otherwise). Separate statements, no surprise.
  local dest="$1" src="$2" tmp
  tmp="$dest.tmp.$$"
  if ! cp "$src" "$tmp"; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: cannot write $dest (copy step failed)"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! mv "$tmp" "$dest"; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: cannot write $dest (rename step failed)"
    return 1
  fi
}

# api_get_json <url> <dest> — GET url into dest as validated JSON.
#   - retries transient network failures (curl --retry-connrefused)
#   - fails on any HTTP error status (curl -f, so a 500/404 body is NOT kept)
#   - refuses to store a 200 body that is not valid JSON (an HTML error page
#     must never end up in the evidence store)
#   - writes dest atomically
# Returns non-zero with a clear stderr line on any failure.
api_get_json() {
  local url="$1" dest="$2" tmp
  tmp="$(mktemp)"
  if ! curl -sfS -m 60 --retry 3 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 2 -o "$tmp" "$url"; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: GET $url failed (HTTP error or host unreachable after retries)"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! jq -e 'type == "object" or type == "array"' "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: GET $url returned a body that is not valid JSON — refusing to store it in $dest"
    return 1
  fi
  # Propagate the write result explicitly: without this, the status of the
  # `rm` below would mask a failed store and the caller would trust a file
  # that was never written.
  local write_rc=0
  write_atomic "$dest" "$tmp" || write_rc=$?
  rm -f "$tmp"
  return "$write_rc"
}

# validate_label <label> — recount/snapshot labels become file- and directory
# names (recount-<label>.jsonl, raw/<label>/...), so they must be a single
# safe path segment. Without this a label like "../../x" would write evidence
# outside the task folder.
validate_label() {
  local label="$1"
  if ! [[ "$label" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ ]]; then
    die "bad label '$label' — use letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore only, starting with a letter or digit (e.g. before, mid-1431)"
  fi
}

# validate_task_prefix <prefix...> — task ids/prefixes get interpolated into
# shell commands (locally and over ssh) by e5-sweep.sh, so they must be hex
# and dashes only. Accepts a short prefix (8 hex chars) or a full UUID.
# This is the injection guard for the sweep: anything else is rejected before
# any command runs.
validate_task_prefix() {
  local p
  for p in "$@"; do
    if ! [[ "$p" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}(-[0-9a-fA-F]{4,12})*$ ]]; then
      die "bad task id prefix '$p' — expected 8 hex chars plus optional -hex groups (e.g. 7f6220c3 or the full UUID)"
    fi
  done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — record the fleet matrix
# (GET /runners + GET /deploy/status) and a per-runner convergence verdict.
# READ-ONLY against the backend; safe to run any time, any number of times.
#
# Outputs in <outdir>:
#   runners-<stamp>.json        raw GET /runners payload (evidence)
#   runners-<stamp>.tsv         flat fleet table incl. build sha/builtAt
#   deploy-status-<stamp>.json  raw GET /deploy/status payload
#   verdict-<stamp>.txt         one line per named runner: CONVERGED or the reasons why not
#
# Convergence rule (S5 success criterion 1): runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND the
# running build's reported git sha contains the fix commit — verified locally
# with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fixCommit> <buildSha>`, because a version
# string alone cannot prove which code is running. If the runner reports no
# build sha, the verdict says so instead of guessing.
#
# Knobs (env):
#   KAINBAIN_API_BASE            default http://192.168.1.206:3100
#   KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS    default "local-alpha,server2-alpha"
#   KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT       default 046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4 (the 046a6391 deterministic-git-failure change)
#
# Exit codes: 0 snapshot written (converged or not — read verdict-<stamp>.txt);
#   1 setup or API failure (nothing trustworthy written);
#   3 snapshot written, --require-converged given, but not all named runners converged.
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

# fix_in_build <buildSha|""|null> — prints true/false/null. null = cannot tell
# (no sha reported, or sha unknown to the local repo). Uses the local Kainbain
# checkout as the commit database — read-only git queries only.
fix_in_build() {
  local sha="$1" repo_root="$2" fix_commit="$3"
  if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ "$sha" = "null" ]; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if ! git -C "$repo_root" cat-file -e "$sha^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if git -C "$repo_root" merge-base --is-ancestor "$fix_commit" "$sha" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo true
  else
    echo false
  fi
}

# verdict_for <runners.json> <runnerId> — prints the verdict JSON object for one
# runner (jq/runner-verdict.jq + the git ancestry check).
verdict_for() {
  local runners_json="$1" runner_id="$2" repo_root="$3" fix_commit="$4"
  local runner sha fix
  runner="$(jq -c --arg id "$runner_id" '.[] | select(.runnerId == $id) // empty' "$runners_json")"
  if [ -z "$runner" ]; then
    printf '{"runnerId":"%s","converged":false,"reasons":["runner not present in GET /runners (offline/revoked?)"]}\n' "$runner_id"
    return 0
  fi
  sha="$(printf '%s' "$runner" | jq -r '.facts.versions.build.sha // ""')"
  fix="$(fix_in_build "$sha" "$repo_root" "$fix_commit")"
  jq -n -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/runner-verdict.jq" --argjson runner "$runner" --argjson fixInBuild "$fix"
}

main() {
  require_commands curl jq git date mktemp
  local outdir="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$outdir" ] || die "usage: runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged]"
  local require_converged=0
  if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
    [ "$2" = "--require-converged" ] || die "usage: runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — unexpected argument '$2'"
    require_converged=1
  fi
  [ $# -le 2 ] || die "usage: runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — unexpected extra argument '$3'"

  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
  local named="${KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS:-local-alpha,server2-alpha}"
  [ -n "${named//[[:space:],]/}" ] || die "no named runners to check (KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS is empty) — nothing to do"
  local fix_commit="${KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT:-046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4}"
  local task_dir repo_root stamp
  task_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
  repo_root="$(git -C "$task_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
  # Second precision: two snapshots in the same minute must not overwrite each other.
  stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
  mkdir -p "$outdir"

  log "runners-snapshot api=$api_base outdir=$outdir named=$named fix=$fix_commit"

  local runners_json="$outdir/runners-$stamp.json" deploy_json="$outdir/deploy-status-$stamp.json"
  api_get_json "$api_base/runners" "$runners_json" \
    || die "GET $api_base/runners failed — nothing written to $outdir"
  # /runners must be an array of runner objects; anything else (an error
  # envelope, an HTML page that slipped through) would make every downstream
  # verdict meaningless, so stop here with a clear message.
  if ! jq -e 'type == "array"' "$runners_json" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rm -f "$runners_json"
    die "GET $api_base/runners returned valid JSON that is not an array — refusing to build a verdict from it"
  fi
  local deploy_ok=1
  api_get_json "$api_base/deploy/status" "$deploy_json" \
    || { log "WARN: GET /deploy/status failed — continuing with /runners only"; rm -f "$deploy_json"; deploy_ok=0; }

  jq -r -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/runners-tsv.jq" "$runners_json" > "$outdir/runners-$stamp.tsv"

  local verdict_json="$outdir/verdict-$stamp.json" verdict_txt="$outdir/verdict-$stamp.txt"
  local verdict_body
  verdict_body="$(mktemp)"
  : > "$verdict_json.tmp.$$"
  local IFS=',' r all_converged=1 v
  # Named runners come from env, so tolerate "a, b" spacing and stray commas.
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  for r in $named; do
    r="${r//[[:space:]]/}"
    [ -n "$r" ] || continue
    v="$(verdict_for "$runners_json" "$r" "$repo_root" "$fix_commit")"
    printf '%s\n' "$v" >> "$verdict_json.tmp.$$"
    if printf '%s' "$v" | jq -e '.converged == true' >/dev/null; then
      printf 'CONVERGED    %s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$v" | jq -r '[.runnerId, .runnerVersion, (.buildSha // "no-sha")] | join(" ")')" >> "$verdict_body"
    else
      all_converged=0
      printf 'NOT-CONVERGED %s — %s\n' "$r" "$(printf '%s' "$v" | jq -r '.reasons | join("; ")')" >> "$verdict_body"
    fi
  done
  jq -s '.' "$verdict_json.tmp.$$" > "$verdict_json" && rm -f "$verdict_json.tmp.$$"

  {
    echo "# runner convergence verdict — $(date -u +%FT%TZ) — fix commit $fix_commit"
    echo "# converged = runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND running build sha contains the fix commit"
    cat "$verdict_body"
  } > "$verdict_txt" && rm -f "$verdict_body"

  if [ "$deploy_ok" = 1 ]; then
    echo "wrote $outdir/runners-$stamp.{json,tsv} $outdir/deploy-status-$stamp.json $outdir/verdict-$stamp.{json,txt}"
  else
    echo "wrote $outdir/runners-$stamp.{json,tsv} $outdir/verdict-$stamp.{json,txt} (no deploy-status: GET /deploy/status failed)"
  fi
  cat "$outdir/runners-$stamp.tsv"
  echo "--- verdict:"
  cat "$verdict_txt"

  if [ "$require_converged" = 1 ] && [ "$all_converged" = 0 ]; then
    log "--require-converged: not all named runners converged (see $verdict_txt)"
    exit 3
  fi
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# e5-sweep.sh <local|server2> <taskId-prefix>... — GUIDE-05 §4 E5 forensics
# sweep. READ-ONLY: it never reaps, deletes, restarts, updates, or modifies
# anything on either host (survey q9: observe only). For each kb-<taskId>
# it records, per host:
#   - worktrees under the work root: existence + git log + whether a
#     stage-output commit is present in HEAD history
#   - origin branch refs (refs/remotes/origin/kb/<id>* and kb-<id>*): the
#     durable evidence that survives worktree reaping, with git log
#
# Stage-output detection is scoped to the task's OWN branch: a commit counts
# only if its subject matches ^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output. Merged/mirrored
# history regularly contains OTHER tasks' stage-output commits (observed in
# the 2026-11-23 before-sweep: kb/1cae113f commits inside kb/7f6220c3 refs),
# and an unscoped grep would flip the verdict to a false Cause 2/4.
#   - journal lines for the task id (Runner failed / commit / hook / 413 /
#     502 / fetch failed / interrupt)
# and prints one VERDICT line per task:
#   stage-output commit PRESENT  -> Cause 2/4 territory (GUIDE-05 §4)
#   evidence found, commit ABSENT -> Cause 5 suspect (commit/push loop with no landed output)
#   no worktree and no origin ref -> evidence gap (reaped/branch deleted)
#
# Safety: task-id arguments are validated (hex/dashes only — injection guard,
# see lib.sh) and the remote probe is sent base64-encoded, so no argument can
# break out of the remote shell. The probe itself runs only ls/git
# log/for-each-ref/journalctl — all read-only.
#
# Usage:
#   bin/e5-sweep.sh local   7f6220c3 db49d6c6 ...
#   bin/e5-sweep.sh server2 158394ab ...
# Env overrides (used by the test suite, harmless in prod):
#   E5_WORK_ROOT  E5_UNIT  E5_ORIGIN_REPO  E5_JOURNAL_SINCE
# Exit codes: 0 all probed; 1 usage/setup error; 2 some probes failed (output
# still written — the summary says which).
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

# The probe body. Fixed text — the only variables are its five positional
# arguments, all validated or script-controlled before this runs anywhere.
PROBE_SCRIPT='
set -uo pipefail
WORK_ROOT="$1"; UNIT="$2"; ORIGIN_REPO="$3"; PREFIX="$4"; SINCE="$5"
stage_present=0; any_evidence=0

echo "== task kb-$PREFIX"
echo "-- worktrees under $WORK_ROOT:"
found=0
for d in "$WORK_ROOT"/kb-"$PREFIX"*; do
  [ -d "$d" ] || continue
  found=1; any_evidence=1
  echo "   worktree: $d (branch: $(git -C "$d" branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo "?"))"
  git -C "$d" log --format="     %h %ci %s" -5 2>&1 | head -6 || true
  # NB: grep WITHOUT -q on purpose — under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` exits on
  # the first match, git log gets SIGPIPE (rc 141), and the pipeline reports
  # failure even when a match existed. Plain grep reads all input: rc 0 = match.
  if git -C "$d" log --format=%s -20 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output" >/dev/null; then
    stage_present=1
    echo "     stage-output-commit: PRESENT in worktree HEAD history (subject ^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output)"
  else
    echo "     stage-output-commit: absent in worktree HEAD history"
  fi
  for ref in $(git -C "$d" for-each-ref --format="%(refname)" "refs/remotes/origin/kb/$PREFIX"* "refs/remotes/origin/kb-$PREFIX"* 2>/dev/null); do
    echo "   origin ref: $ref"
    git -C "$d" log --format="     %h %ci %s" -5 "$ref" 2>&1 | head -6 || true
    if git -C "$d" log --format=%s -20 "$ref" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output" >/dev/null; then
      stage_present=1
      echo "     stage-output-commit: PRESENT on $ref (subject ^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output)"
    else
      echo "     stage-output-commit: absent on $ref"
    fi
  done
done
[ "$found" = 1 ] || echo "   (no worktree on this host)"

echo "-- origin branch refs in $ORIGIN_REPO (durable, survives worktree reaping):"
if git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  refs=$(git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" for-each-ref --format="%(refname)" "refs/remotes/origin/kb/$PREFIX"* "refs/remotes/origin/kb-$PREFIX"* "refs/heads/kb/$PREFIX"* "refs/heads/kb-$PREFIX"* 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "$refs" ]; then
    any_evidence=1
    while IFS= read -r ref; do
      echo "   $ref"
      git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" log --format="     %h %ci %s" -8 "$ref" 2>&1 | head -9 || true
      if git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" log --format=%s -20 "$ref" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output" >/dev/null; then
        stage_present=1
        echo "     stage-output-commit: PRESENT on $ref (subject ^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output)"
      else
        echo "     stage-output-commit: absent on $ref"
      fi
    done <<EOF
$refs
EOF
  else
    echo "   (no origin branch kb/$PREFIX* or kb-$PREFIX*)"
  fi
else
  echo "   (origin repo $ORIGIN_REPO not available on this host — evidence gap note)"
fi

echo "-- journal ($UNIT, since $SINCE) lines matching $PREFIX:"
if command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  journalctl --user -u "$UNIT" --since "$SINCE" --no-pager 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -i -- "$PREFIX" | grep -iE "Runner failed|commit|hook|413|502|fetch failed|interrupt" | tail -15 | sed "s/^/   /" \
    || echo "   (no matching journal lines)"
else
  echo "   (journalctl not available on this host)"
fi

if [ "$stage_present" = 1 ]; then
  echo "VERDICT kb-$PREFIX: stage-output commit PRESENT -> Cause 2/4 territory (GUIDE-05 §4)"
elif [ "$any_evidence" = 1 ]; then
  echo "VERDICT kb-$PREFIX: evidence found but no stage-output commit -> Cause 5 suspect (commit/push loop, no landed output)"
else
  echo "VERDICT kb-$PREFIX: no worktree and no origin branch -> evidence gap (worktree reaped and branch deleted)"
fi
echo
'

# run_probe <host> <work_root> <unit> <origin_repo> <prefix> <since>
# Local: pipe the probe into bash directly. server2: base64-encode the probe
# and decode it on the remote side, so argument quoting can never inject.
run_probe() {
  local host="$1"; shift
  local args; args="$(printf '%q ' "$@")"
  if [ "$host" = "server2" ]; then
    local b64
    b64="$(printf '%s' "$PROBE_SCRIPT" | base64 -w0)"
    "$SCRIPT_DIR/server2-ssh.sh" "echo $b64 | base64 -d | bash -s -- $args"
  else
    printf '%s' "$PROBE_SCRIPT" | bash -s -- "$@"
  fi
}

main() {
  require_commands bash base64 date git
  local host="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$host" ] || die "usage: e5-sweep.sh <local|server2> <taskId-prefix>..."
  [ "$host" = "local" ] || [ "$host" = "server2" ] || die "host must be 'local' or 'server2', got '$host'"
  shift
  [ $# -ge 1 ] || die "usage: e5-sweep.sh <local|server2> <taskId-prefix>... (at least one task id)"
  validate_task_prefix "$@"

  local task_dir repo_root work_root unit origin_repo since
  task_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
  repo_root="$(git -C "$task_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
  since="${E5_JOURNAL_SINCE:-2026-11-19}"
  if [ "$host" = "server2" ]; then
    work_root="${E5_WORK_ROOT:-/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work}"
    unit="${E5_UNIT:-kainbain-runner-server2-alpha}"
    origin_repo="${E5_ORIGIN_REPO:-/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/mirrors/Kainbain}"
  else
    work_root="${E5_WORK_ROOT:-$HOME/.kainbain/runner-work}"
    unit="${E5_UNIT:-kainbain-runner-local-alpha}"
    origin_repo="${E5_ORIGIN_REPO:-$repo_root}"
  fi

  echo "## E5 sweep host=$host work_root=$work_root unit=$unit origin_repo=$origin_repo since=$since at $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  local failed=0 t
  for t in "$@"; do
    if ! run_probe "$host" "$work_root" "$unit" "$origin_repo" "$t" "$since"; then
      failed=$((failed + 1))
      log "WARN: probe for kb-$t on $host failed — recorded, continuing with the next task"
      echo "VERDICT kb-$t: PROBE FAILED on $host (see stderr) — treat as evidence gap"
      echo
    fi
  done
  echo "## E5 sweep done: $# task(s), $failed probe failure(s) at $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
    log "exiting 2: $failed probe(s) failed"
    exit 2
  fi
}

if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
  main "$@"
fi

# fleet-recount.sh <label> [task-dir] — GUIDE-07 §5 fleet recount +
# WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table, over one project, read-only against the
